categories.label: Art & Galleries
categories.description: Contemporary art galleries, studios and street art. Programmes move in months rather than weeks, so most of this category is harvested monthly.

categories.label: Cinema
categories.description: Independent and commercial cinemas, plus film festivals and pop-up screenings.

categories.label: City-wide
categories.description: Cross-category listings sites, the council and the tourist board. These are the safety net: anything the category catalogues miss — pop-ups, one-off community events, venue-less happenings — tends to surface here first.

categories.label: Comedy
categories.description: Comedy clubs, improv, and the venues whose comedy programme is substantial enough to be worth watching on its own.

categories.label: Learning & Talks
categories.description: Public lectures, adult education and outreach — the programmes whose purpose is that someone leaves knowing something. A university publishing its own public programme belongs here rather than among the city-wide aggregators, which is why `education/university-of-bristol` was re-homed out of `citywide`. UWE stays there for now: unlike Bristol's, its entry has real harvest history behind it.

categories.label: Family & Kids
categories.description: City farms, play spaces and companies producing for children. Programmes spike hard in school holidays, which is the main thing to get right here.

categories.label: Festivals
categories.description: Annual, mostly venue-less events. The largest things that happen in the city live here, and almost none of them appear on any venue's website. Announcements cluster in winter and spring for a summer that sells out early.

categories.label: Food & Drink
categories.description: Food halls, breweries and taprooms with public event programmes. Only sources that actually programme events belong here — a restaurant with no events is not a source, however good it is.

categories.label: Gardens & Horticulture
categories.description: Botanic gardens, nurseries, growing projects and open-garden schemes. Sharply seasonal: plant fairs and open days cluster in spring and early summer, and most of this category has nothing on at all in January.

categories.label: Literature & Talks
categories.description: Bookshops with event programmes, literary festivals, spoken word and poetry nights, and public talks.

categories.label: Making & Craft
categories.description:
Makerspaces, workshops, printmaking, woodwork and craft courses.
The distinctive problem in this category is that most listings are *courses*, not events — a ten-week evening class is not the same thing as a one-off workshop, and a "what's on" page is much less useful if it fills up with enrolment listings. Prefer one-off and short workshops, open days and public makes; record a recurring course as `occurrence.kind: recurring` with the pattern stated, rather than as a stream of dated events.

categories.label: Markets
categories.description: Street and indoor markets. Almost all are `occurrence.kind: recurring` — a weekly or monthly pattern rather than dated events — which makes them a good test of that part of the schema.

categories.label: Museums & Heritage
categories.description: Museums, heritage sites and science centres. Mostly permanent collections (`occurrence.kind: ongoing`) punctuated by temporary exhibitions and events.

categories.label: Music
categories.description: Concert halls, grassroots venues, club spaces and the promoters who programme them. Bristol's densest category by volume.

categories.label: Parks & Outdoors
categories.description: Estates, woods and green space that host public events. These are places before they are venues — most of the year they have no programme at all, and then a single weekend brings fifty thousand people.

categories.label: Sport
categories.description: Professional clubs and their grounds. Fixtures are published a season at a time and then move for TV, so the value here is in re-checking dates rather than discovering new events.

categories.label: Theatre
categories.description: Playhouses, studio theatres, circus and physical theatre, and the companies that programme into other people's spaces.

Join us for a tour of the stunning Blaise Museum!

Let us introduce you to our grand historic house, share some stories you won't find

Whether you're a seasoned Bristolian or a curious newcomer, we hope to inspire and
leave you with a deeper appreciation for the treasures housed within Blaise Museum.

events.timesText: Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays – 11:30am and 2pm (approx. 30 minutes)

price.text: Standard ticket £5; under 16s free; carer/sighted guide free

events.raw:
1 April—31 December 2026

TOUR: Join us on an exploratory tour of the Georgian House Museum, learning about the
history of the house and the people who lived there.
events.summary: Half an hour across four floors of a 230-year-old town house, taking in both Georgian domestic life and the slave-trade wealth that paid for it.
events.description:
Join us on an exploratory tour of the Georgian House Museum, learning about the history
of the house and the people who lived there.

Through the lens of a single household, guests will learn, not only about day-to-day
life in Georgian times, but about the dramatic and harrowing global events which
fuelled an era of both prosperity and tragedy, technology and romance, tradition and
progress.

Tours are approximately 30 minutes long. Visitors will be taken on a brief historical
journey throughout four floors of the 230 year old Georgian town house. You can book a
tour online up to two days before the event; box office tickets may be available to buy
on the day (subject to availability). Please arrive no more than five minutes early to
avoid having to wait around outside.

Eating and drinking (with the exception of bottled water) is not permitted inside the
museum.

Be aware that the tour deals with more difficult themes relating to the house's
colonial past and involvement with the trafficking of enslaved Africans which some
visitors may find distressing.

**Accessibility** — The number of stairs in the museum mean that the tour is not
accessible for those with reduced mobility.

**Facilities** — There is no access to toilet facilities on premises.

**Tours start:** Fridays 11:30am and 2pm; Saturdays 11:30am and 2pm; Sundays 11:30am
and 2pm.

events.raw:
19 June – 20 September 2026

**Walking Brunel's Bristol** — Join Mr B on a historic walking tour of Bristol's
harbourside.
events.summary: Three miles round the Floating Harbour in the company of Brunel himself, taking in Underfall Yard, Cumberland Basin and Queen Square over two and a quarter hours.
events.description:
Join Mr B on a historic walking tour of Bristol's harbourside.

Unearth the stories, mishaps and mayhem behind Brunel's legacy, and discover how the city
of Bristol helped to forge one of history's greatest engineers.

Covering just over 3 miles of the harbourside, the tours last approximately 2 hrs 15 mins
and commence and finish outside The Board Walk restaurant in Brunel Square — located just
outside the main entrance to Bristol Dockyards.

Primarily following a circular route around Bristol's Floating Harbour, Mr. Brunel will
discuss his Bristol born projects, tales from his own life, the history of the harbour as
well as some interesting chapters from Bristol's past and present. Main stops on the tour
include Underfall Yard, Cumberland Basin, Queen Square and of course, the SS Great Britain.

**Tickets** — Online advance booking only, subject to capacity. Dates available: August —
Sun 9, Fri 14, Sun 23, Mon 31. September — Sun 6, Fri 11, Sun 20. General Admission to the
site is not included, however an Afternoon Saver can be added to your ticket.

**Key info** — Time: 10.30am–12.45pm. Please arrive 15 minutes before the tour is
scheduled to depart; Mr. Brunel is a stickler for timekeeping. Price: £14.00. Suitable for
families, 8 and over, neurodiverse visitors and travellers.

The tour is designed to be fully accessible for mobility scooters and wheelchairs, with
one or two small inclines and occasional cobbles. There are no scheduled toilet or picnic
stops, though public toilets are located en route. Dogs are welcome on a lead. Booking
changes can be made up to 24 hours in advance, but tickets are not refundable.

events.title: Folly
events.raw:
**Folly** — 23 June - 30 August 2026. Kenny Gallery, RWA, Queens Road,
Bristol, BS8 1PX. Admission free. Tuesday - Sunday: 10am - 5pm (Closed
Mondays).
events.summary: Four RWA Academicians, curated by Peter Burke, on folly in every sense: the ornamental towers and mock ruins of the eighteenth century, the obsolete monuments of modern ideology, and the private project pursued against all logic. Free, and in its final fortnight.
events.description:
Curated by Peter Burke RWA, with works by Peter Burke RWA, Judith Jones
RWA, Jemma Gunning RWA RE and Karl Singporewala RWA RIBA.

The exhibition explores folly through several lenses. It looks at the
tradition of folly building that emerged centuries ago in Britain,
where wealthy individuals chose to demonstrate their prosperity by
commissioning ornamental structures, often as towers or mock ruins. It
asks whether modern structures shaped by political, religious or
commercial ideologies, now redundant or obsolete, constitute
contemporary follies. And it explores the urge to undertake an
idiosyncratic project for its own sake, flying in the face of logic.

Across a wide range of mediums, these themes run as a common thread for
contemporary artistic exploration.

Kenny Gallery, RWA, Queens Road, Bristol, BS8 1PX. Admission free.
Tuesday – Sunday: 10am – 5pm, closed Mondays.

events.title: If Schools Were Ours to Imagine
events.raw:
**If Schools Were Ours to Imagine** — 1 Jul 2026 – 2 Jan 2027, Open City Lab. Recommended
for families.

Head to our Open City Lab, get creative and add to our evolving exhibition exploring how
schools could be made fairer for everyone.
events.summary: A growing exhibition made by its visitors, built with Oxford's Repair-Ed project on class and racial inequality in Bristol schools — retro desks to smell and hear, clay models, bunting, and an interactive city map of school memories.
events.description:
What would it look like if we could decide what schools were like in future? Get creative
and add to our evolving exhibition exploring how schools could be made fairer for everyone.

There are six mini-activities in the space:

- Head to the retro desks and smell, touch, and listen to connect with local Bristolian's
  memories of school.
- It's school dance time. Express how people's stories of school make you feel through
  movement.
- Make a clay model of what would you add to school to make it better (fairer)?
- If you could do anything on your dream school day, what would it be? Decorate a piece of
  bunting to add to the display.
- Share your thoughts and reflections on what you've experienced in the space, and your own
  school stories. Write it down or record it with the team.
- Explore an interactive map of Bristol with stories from the repair-ed archive.

This project is in partnership with Reparative Futures of Education (Repair-Ed) from the
University of Oxford. This collaboration builds on the team's existing work which explores
people's experiences of schooling in relation to racial and class inequality in Bristol and
how schools could be made fairer in future.

**Access considerations** — This activity takes place in a slightly enclosed ground floor
space that is wheelchair accessible with a lot of room between tables and information stands.

events.title: 1000 Years of Fashion History – an exhibition in miniature
events.raw:
18 July—1 November 2026

EXHIBITION: A timeline in miniature, with more than 100 hand-made costumes modelled
by fashion dolls.
events.summary: A thousand years of British dress rebuilt at doll scale — more than a hundred hand-sewn costumes made over six years by former theatre costumier Lisa Jayne Smith.
events.description:
From Saxon robes to Elizabethan ruffs, Victorian tartan and punk piercings, come and
see how what we wear has changed across time… in miniature!

This exhibition has been created by Lisa Jayne Smith, following a career working in
theatre and running her own business making and adapting period costume. She has been
an avid fan of costume history for as long as she can remember, and the exhibition is
inspired by a book she came across while costuming for a play, 'The Change in Fashion
from 1066-1960s'.

Lisa spent six years researching and making more than 100 miniature historical
costumes while receiving treatment for breast cancer. Each hand made outfit, modelled
by a 12-inch fashion doll, is complete down to the tiniest detail. The amount of time
spent on each model would depend on the size and era of each costume, anything from a
week to a month.

Journey through time, from the Saxons through Medieval, Renaissance, Tudor,
Elizabethan, Jacobean, Carolean, Restoration, Stuart, Georgian, Victorian, Edwardian,
1910's, 1920's, 1930's, 1940's, 1950's, 1960's, 1970's up to the 1980's.

"I hope you enjoy looking at them as much as I have in making and creating them!" —
Lisa Jayne Smith

This exhibition is located in the first floor costume gallery, please be aware there
are only stairs to this floor, no lift is available. Suitable for children of all
ages. Drop in, no booking necessary. Free, donations welcome.

events.title: Conservation Carnival!
events.raw:
**Conservation Carnival!** — 18 July – 31 August

Celebrate the incredible conservation success stories helping to protect our oceans
and wildlife this summer at Bristol Aquarium.
events.summary: The aquarium's summer programme, hung on six species and the projects keeping them going — a stamp trail, daily guided tours, a beachcombing sandpit and a conservation corner, all on the standard ticket.
events.description:
Celebrate the incredible conservation success stories helping to protect our oceans and
wildlife this summer at Bristol Aquarium.

Join us for Conservation Carnival, where you'll discover inspiring stories of species
recovery, habitat restoration and the amazing work of conservation charities making a
real difference around the world. Through interactive activities, guided tours and
family-friendly experiences, you'll learn how small actions can help protect our blue
planet.

**Take on the Conservation Trail** — Collect stamps as you journey through the
aquarium, discovering six fascinating species and the conservation projects helping
them thrive.

**Daily Save Our Seas Guided Tours – 11am** — Join our expert team each day for a free
guided conservation tour through a different area of the aquarium. Discover amazing
animal facts, learn about the challenges these species face in the wild and hear
inspiring stories of conservation success. Tours last approximately 15–20 minutes and
include time for questions.

**Treasure or Trash: Sandpit Search – Daily at 4pm** — Become a marine explorer as you
dig through our interactive beach combing sandpit. Discover fascinating natural
treasures including shark teeth, shark egg cases, fossils, seashells, coral fragments
and ancient marine specimens. You'll also uncover examples of plastic pollution and
learn why keeping our beaches clean is so important for marine wildlife.

**Visit the Conservation Corner** — Looking for ways to make a difference after your
visit? Our Conservation Corner is packed with ideas for the whole family, including
beach clean information, conservation charities you can support, how Bristol Aquarium
and Aspro Parks help protect wildlife, and children's colouring activities.

All Conservation Carnival activities are included with standard aquarium admission.
Come along this summer and be inspired by the positive impact people are making to
protect our oceans—then discover how you can be part of the story.

**Ships and Giggles** — A summer of games, adventure and silliness down at the Dockyards.
events.summary: Summer challenges drawn from the ship's own history — jar fishing as child passengers did it, giant jump rope, orders bellowed through the engine-room speaking trumpets, and a pie race off an 1863 menu.
events.description:
Pack up your playmates and set sail for fun.

This summer at Bristol Dockyards – home of SS Great Britain – we're bringing the stories
of one of the world's most extraordinary ships to life through games, challenges and a
whole lot of laughs.

From the dockside to the dining room, take part in interactive challenges inspired by the
SS Great Britain's global voyages. Here's a taste of what's in store:

- **Jar Fishing:** Child passengers would dangle jars into the sea to catch fish – without
  even being able to see what they'd caught! Now it's your turn.
- **Jump Rope:** Swing into action with our giant jump rope – a favourite from the streets
  of New York City. How long can you keep going?
- **Good Shout:** Head down to the engine room and listen out for your orders – called out
  through the speaking trumpets just like the real crew. How many commands can you get
  right?
- **Who Made All the Pies?** Race to make three fruit pies in the ship's galley before
  anyone else! Flip cards to build your desserts, based on a real menu from 1863.

**Key info** — Time: 10:00am-5:00pm. Price: included in your ticket.

**Kids Go Free — all summer long:** one child free for every paying adult, from now until
2 September. Come back as many times as you like at no extra cost: one ticket, a whole year
of adventures.

events.description:
A tour of travels and tales! Join one of our costume characters for a unique guided tour
aboard the SS Great Britain and discover the amazing true stories of people who sailed on
the ship that changed the world.

Find out what life was really like on board the most famous Victorian steamship and marvel
at the experiences of those who dared to venture across the world in search of fame,
fortune and fresh beginnings.

Led by a Victorian costume guide, the tour will last 50 minutes and cover all three decks
of the SS Great Britain. Online booking is recommended, though tickets can be purchased in
house, subject to capacity on the day. Tickets are available until 1pm on the day of the
tour, however we advise people to please arrive at the stern of the ship 10 minutes before
their tour.

**Key info** — Tickets: £5pp (all ages). Annual Ticket Holders can buy tickets separately;
otherwise, you can add your Voyager Voices Tour to your General Admission booking. Dates:
Tue, Thu, Sat and Sun between 21 Jul - 30 Aug. NB: Tue 11 Aug will be held on Fri 14 Aug

events.raw:
**Summer Kitchen** — 23 Jul – 31 Oct 2026, Kitchen. Recommended for families, best for ages
5-10. Allergens.

Join us for a variety of summery experiments in the Kitchen, from our Big Green Grill-Off
to cool sorbet making.
events.summary: Three rotating food-chemistry experiments at the kitchen counter — invent a meat-free burger, freeze sorbet with salt, or force oil and water together into mayonnaise.
events.description:
This summer we've got three fun activities in the kitchen, all delving into food chemistry
and how we can eat sustainably.

Learn a bit more about what our food is made of and some of the hidden chemistry that goes
in to cooking, have a fun tasting experience and learn some new foody skills to try at home!

**Activities on offer:**

- **The Big Green Grill-Off** — Love a BBQ? Not sure about all the meat? Become a
  sustainable chef as you invent and cook your own meat-free burgers.
- **Supercool Sorbet** — How can salt help things freeze? Use some clever chemistry to make
  sorbet in minutes.
- **Will it Mix?** — We've heard that oil and water don't mix but, with a bit of science, we
  reckon they might. It's time to get saucy – and make some mayonnaise!

Activities running will vary depending on term time verses weekends and holidays. Please
always check the activity screens on arrival to see which activities are running at what
time each day.

**Accessibility / allergens** — This activity takes place on a raised kitchen counter. When
the venue is busy, you may need to share space and equipment with other visitors. Allergens
include milk, eggs and gluten though the activity can be adapted. Please speak to a member
of staff about any allergies before taking part.

Enjoy a summer day out packed with hands-on activities, live shows, storytelling and

events.summary: The whole summer holiday programme in one listing — an Investigation Station challenge, food chemistry in the Kitchen, a shadow-play studio, the schools exhibition and sensory storytelling, all on one day ticket you can leave and re-enter.
events.description:
Looking for summer holiday activities for the family?

Summer of Imagination is our summer holiday programme packed with hands-on science,
creative workshops and drop-in experiences for all ages. All activities are included with
your admission ticket unless otherwise stated.

Your ticket lasts all day, meaning you can come and go as you please, popping out for ice
creams and sunshine, and then back into the cool.

**Summer holiday activities** — Fly through the rings of Saturn, explore illusions and
magic tricks, find rainbows, make fruit sorbets – there's so much to see and do.

- **Investigation Station (Theatre of Curiosity):** Swing by the station for our daily
  challenge. Will you be imagining life as early man or exploring invisibility through
  magic tricks?
- **Summer Kitchen (The Kitchen):** Experiment with food science as you make instant fruit
  sorbets and explore alternatives to traditional ingredients.
- **Shadow Factory (The Studio):** Play with light, colour and shadow as you create
  mosaics, experiment with shapes and bring your own shadow stories to life.
- **If Schools Were Ours to Imagine (Open City Lab):** Explore with us and share your ideas
  for a fairer future by adding thoughts, designs and creative contributions to this
  evolving exhibition.
- **Storytelling (The Studio):** Join Ursa and Leo for a sensory storytelling adventure
  filled with colour, imagination and opportunities to join in. Recommended for children
  under 7.

**Good to know** — All activities are drop-in. Check activity times when you arrive.

Please note, our Theatre of Curiosity will be closed from Wed 22 - Fri 24 July for
essential maintenance. The Investigation Station will be running from Sat 25 July onwards.

events.description:
We know that venues like ours can sometimes be overwhelming, so on Relaxed Mornings our
experience looks a little different.

These mornings have been specifically designed for visitors who may need a little extra
support to enjoy our venue. This may be due to disability or neurodiversity, such as autism
or other sensory processing conditions.

The session runs from 10.00am -12.00pm, with the building gradually getting busier from 12.30
onwards. Your ticket is valid for the whole day and you can come and go as you wish, just
keep hold of your ticket to show our team when you re-enter.

**Upcoming Relaxed Mornings:** Sunday 2 August 2026 (Summer Holidays); Sunday 4 October 2026;
Sunday 6 December 2026; Sunday 7 February 2027.

**Access considerations** — Visitor numbers are restricted during these events, to ensure
there is plenty of space to play. The sounds of some of our noisier exhibits are lowered. Our
Live Science team are on hand to offer a warm welcome and support you during your visit. The
Planetarium is free and drop-in, rather than ticketed – meaning you can stay for as long (or
as little) as you want.

events.description:
The Great Bristol Ball Run is landing on Millennium Square and Anchor Square from 4 Aug!

Pick up a wooden ball for £6 in our We The Curious shop and let the fun begin.

There'll be 6 different ball runs dotted around the squares for you to try out. Including
one run as tall as a double decker bus, featuring an overhead wire run and Archimedes screw
lift. There'll also be tilting mazes, skittle alleys and head-to-head racing challenges.

Once you've had a go, the ball is yours to keep as a souvenir, and you can bring it back and
play as many times as you like!

Each ball is crafted from sustainably sourced British ash at a solar-powered workshop in
Somerset, by the team behind some of the UK's best-loved outdoor ball run experiences,
including those at the Eden Project and Forestry England sites. At just £6, take your wooden
ball home as a keepsake once you're done — or come back tomorrow and run it all again.

Pick up a ball. Head outside with the fam. See you at the Ball Run!

A series of special activities happening in our Test-Lab this summer.
events.summary: Four drop-in sessions where university researchers bring live work into the Test-Lab — editing a children's book about AI, growing furniture, quantum computing, and designing for smell and taste.
events.description:
From Quantum computing to Bio-engineering we've got a series of special events in the
Test-Lab this summer. Our research partners will be coming down to join us and you can get
involved with some exciting real-life research. All events are included in your day ticket.

**Events coming up:**

- **Wed 5 Aug: Help write a book!** Get a sneak peak and help edit a book about AI for
  children written by researchers at the University of Bristol. Activity is drop in between
  11am and 2.30pm.
- **Tues 18 Aug: Bio-engineering future furniture.** What if you could plant a seed and grow
  a chair? Join researchers to explore and share your thoughts on the future of objects
  living, non-living and somewhere in between. Activity is drop in between 11am and 1pm.
- **Tues 25 Aug: Quantum computing.** How could the invisible world of quantum phenomena
  change our lives in future? What exactly is quantum entanglement and what does it have to
  do with computers? Explore these questions and more with this drop-in activity between
  11am and 1pm.
- **Fri 28 Aug: Multisensory design challenge.** What if your smartwatch had a scent? Or
  your phone had a taste? Join us in exploring future alternative interfaces. Discover how
  touch, smell, taste, and other underused senses can inspire more creative, engaging, and
  accessible ways to interact with technology. Activity is drop in between 11am and 1pm.

**Access considerations** — This activity takes place in a slightly enclosed first floor
space that is wheelchair accessible with some room between tables and information stands.
It's led by a facilitator capable of being responsive to audience needs and making reasonable
adjustments.

events.description:
*Journey 3.0* is a joint exhibition showcasing collaborative and
independent works by artists Anna Perra and Tony Church.

Since 2021 the two have developed an artistic partnership exploring
abstract and expressive painting through an intuitive dialogue between
shape, form, colour and movement. Their paintings are bold
compositions with energetic mark-making and vibrant colour palettes,
built up through layers of colour, dynamic forms and expressive
gestures.

Their work has been exhibited in Italy, Spain and England, including
at La Pedrera – Casa Milà in Barcelona, and they contribute to
charitable initiatives through their creative practice. While each
maintains an individual identity, the collaborative pieces represent a
unique exchange of ideas, perspectives and processes.

events.timesText: 11am—12:30pm, except the Community Garden tours at 2pm—3pm
events.raw:
15 August—22 October 2026

WALKS: A special programme of walks designed to explore the Blaise Estate and
celebrate 100 years of public ownership.
events.summary: Five ranger- and volunteer-led walks marking a century of public ownership, each on a different theme — archaeology, wildlife, Repton's landscape, the churchyard and areas normally closed off.
events.description:
A special programme of walks designed to explore the Blaise Estate and celebrate 100
years of public ownership.

Each walk focuses on an aspect of the estate's rich wildlife, its historical
connections or its archaeological discoveries. Walk leaders will take you for a gentle
stroll to different parts of the park sharing what makes the Blaise Estate so special.

**Hidden Blaise** — Join the estate rangers for a guided tour around the estate and
visit areas usually closed to the public. Dates: Sunday 25 October. Time: 11am–12:30pm.

**Blaise Community Garden** — A guided tour around the Community Garden to learn about
the history of the site and how its changed over the years. If you want to discover
how a thriving community garden works then this is the tour for you! Dates: Saturday 15
August, Saturday 19 September. Times: 2pm to 3pm.

**Archaeology and wildlife** — Join the team from Blaise Museum and the Bristol
Regional Environmental Records Centre (BRERC) to find out more about Blaise's
archaeological discoveries and rich wildlife. Dates: Thursday 10 September. Time:
11am–12:30pm.

**Humphrey Repton's landscape** — Join the team from Blaise Museum and explore the
picturesque parkland created for the Harford Family by the famous landscape designer
Humphrey Repton. Dates: Thursday 8 October. Time: 11am–12:30pm.

**St Mary's Church and churchyard** — A guided walk exploring St Mary's church and
churchyard. Learn about the history of this amazing space, the historic memorials and
its links to Bristol's merchant history. Dates: Thursday 22 October. Time:
11am–12:30pm.

All walks last around 90 minutes and start from Blaise Museum unless otherwise stated.
Please arrive at least five minutes before the start of the walk. Suitable outdoor
clothing and a bottle of water are recommended. This event may have to be cancelled at
short notice due external factors such as weather conditions. Tours will go ahead in
wet weather unless the conditions are extreme. Well behaved dogs on leads are only
permitted on walks that specify this in the information above.

Free, donations welcome. Booking essential.

**Noodle+Kin Presents: Mini Atelier School** — Monday 17 to Friday 21
August 2026, 10:00–16:00. "A creativity-led summer holiday club for

events.summary: A week-long summer holiday club for 5-to-8s built around open-ended art, outdoor atelier sessions and expert-led visual arts workshops, closing with a Friday exhibition of the children's work.
events.description:
A creativity-led summer holiday club for children aged 5 to 8.

A joyful week of open-ended art, creative play and outdoor atelier
practice, designed to build confidence, community and connection.

At Mini Atelier School, children will explore open-ended art,
creative play and experimental making through daily Open Studio
sessions.

They will also take part in expert-led visual arts workshops with
Let's Make Art, exploring themes inspired by the natural world. Each
day includes Outdoor Atelier time, where children take their creative
practice outside.

To close the week, families are invited to a Friday exhibition
celebrating the children's work, ideas and creative process.

- Ages – 5 to 8 years
- Times – 10am to 4pm
- Early drop-off – From 9am, £5 per day
- Late pick-up – Until 5pm, £6 per day, Monday to Thursday only
- Location – The Mill Room, St Anne's House, St Anne's Road,
  Brislington, Bristol, BS4 4AB
- Capacity – 23 places total
- Staff ratio – 1:8
- 5-day programme – £250, Monday to Friday
- 3-day programme – £150, Tuesday to Thursday

There is no late pick-up on Friday, as families are invited to the
final exhibition from 4pm to 5pm.

What children will gain:

**Creative skills** — Painting, printmaking, collage, clay,
photography and sculpture.

**Time to go deeper** — Space to develop larger-scale creative
projects across the week.

**Community and confidence** — Opportunities to work alongside other
children, share ideas and build connection.

**Nature-led inspiration** — Daily time outside, using the natural
world to inform the creative process.

**Pride and ownership** — Children will help prepare the final Friday
exhibition and share their work with families.

events.title: Youth Event: A Beginner's Guide to Moth Trapping
events.timesText: Part one, online: Wednesday 19 August 6:00pm–7:00pm. Part two, in person at Grow Wilder: Thursday 20 August 9:00am–10:30am
events.ageRestriction: 14–25 year olds; anyone under 18 must have parental consent to attend. Parents and siblings also welcome.
events.raw:
**Youth Event: A Beginner's Guide to Moth Trapping**

Wednesday 19 August 2026 – Thursday 20 August 2026, 6:00pm – 10:30am. Grow
Wilder, Bristol.

"Join us online to learn about moth trapping and see how to set a trap - and
then come along to see what we catch overnight!"
events.summary:
A two-part crash course in moths for 14- to 25-year-olds: an hour online on
Wednesday evening covering what moths are and how a trap works, then an early
start at Grow Wilder on Thursday to open the trap and identify the catch.
events.description:
Have you ever thought that moths are just drab butterflies? That the only thing
they do is eat holes in your clothes? This 2-part crash course in moths will
prove you wrong!

Part one, online, Wednesday 19 August, 6:00pm–7:00pm: the variety of moths, how
they differ from butterflies, why they matter ecologically, and how to set a
trap.

Part two, in person at Grow Wilder, Thursday 20 August, 9:00am–10:30am:
examining what the trap caught overnight and identifying the species found.

This event is part of our Youth Programme so we ask anyone attending to be
between 14-25 years old. Anyone under 18 must have parental consent to attend.
Parents and siblings are also welcome.

events.summary:

events.description:
Come along to our new weekly summer sessions at Grow Wilder to experience some
of the wonderful wildlife found at our urban nature reserve!

In this session we'll be carrying out a bioblitz at Green Shoots, spreading out
to discover and record as much wildlife as we can! We'll be looking at insects,
plants, birds, reptiles and checking for any signs of mammals too — and we'll
discuss why bioblitzes are so useful.

This will be an active session in an outdoor space, and will take place no
matter the weather — so dress for the weather!

This event is suitable for young people from any level of knowledge or
experience! Come along and say hello, meet new people and learn a new skill.

Grow Wilder, 181 Frenchay Park Road, Bristol, BS16 1EL — reachable on Metrobus
M1, M3 or M4 from the city centre. Parents and siblings are also welcome.

events.title: Loose Ends Jam
events.timesText: 19:00-23:00; beginner lessons run until roughly 21:30, then merge with the general jam
events.summary: A rope-tying jam built around skill-sharing, with two suspension points and experienced people on hand. A separate beginners' tuition ticket covers fundamental harnesses and transitions; for August they strongly recommend bringing a partner, and require one for the lesson.
events.description:
A welcoming event focused on connection, creativity, and skill-sharing.
Two ticket options: **Jam only** and **Jam + Tuition**.

The jam gives space for self-led tying, collaborative exploration, or
learning through observation and exchange, with 2 suspension points
available and support from more experienced folk in the room.

The tuition is aimed at absolute beginners who have never touched rope
before, and at those with some experience who want to refine their
foundations. Teaching covers fundamental harnesses, transitions
(linking ties together), and building confidence and flow.

For August's session the organisers strongly recommend attending with a
partner, and consider it a requirement for anyone wishing to take part
in the lesson. Beginner lessons run until roughly 9:30pm, at which
point they merge with the general jam.

Snacks, water, tea and coffee and communal rope are provided.

Thursday 20 August, 6:00 pm to 8:00 pm.

events.description:
Rest under a shady tree and take up your pencils! On Thursday 20th August,
come down to the University of Bristol Botanic Garden for an evening of
sketching and creatively exploring some of the city's long-lived trees.

We'll wander beneath the branches, drawing and imagining the histories and
memories of some very old trees – from a tightly coiled twisted hazel, to a
giant 400 year old oak.

This session is relaxed and beginner-friendly! Alison will guide and
facilitate, offering prompts and moments to rest, refresh and have a chat.
Drawing materials provided, although you are welcome to bring your own if
you'd prefer.

Arrival 5:45pm for a 6pm start, with 2 comfort breaks. Run by Alison Jones,
independent community engagement practitioner and co-producer of Friendly
Neighbourhood Films. Tickets via Headfirst Bristol; enquiries to
hello.neat.picture@gmail.com.

events.title: FOLKHOUSE PRIDE EXHIBITION: A CELEBRATION POETRY NIGHT
events.raw:
**FOLKHOUSE PRIDE EXHIBITION: A CELEBRATION POETRY NIGHT** — Thursday
20 August 2026, doors 18:30, performances from 19:30. Free with an
optional donation; all proceeds to Dandelion-DIY. Headliners Aish
Humphreys and Edson Burton, hosted by Tom Denbigh, with an open mic.
The event page's own copy reads "Thursday 21st August", which is a
Friday — the listing date of Thursday 20 August is what I have taken.
events.summary: The closing night of the Folk House's queer art exhibition — two headline poets, Aish Humphreys and Edson Burton, an open mic, and donations going to Dandelion-DIY.
events.description:
**FOLKHOUSE PRIDE EXHIBITION: A CELEBRATION | Thursday 21st August
Doors: 6:30pm Performances from 7:30pm**

Join us for a night of flowing words and crafted lyricism as we bring
the Folkhouse Summer Queer Art exhibition to a close.

Featuring two headliners — the impeccable **Aish Humphreys** and the
inimitable **Edson Burton** — expect a night of queer poetry
surrounded by the brilliant artwork featured in our Pride open call,
and of course an open mic with an warm invitation to get involved.

The celebration will be hosted by notoriously queer poet Tom Denbigh,
tickets are free, with an option to donate, and all proceeds will go
directly to Dandelion-DIY. A little more about our headliners:

**Aish Humpries**

Aish is a poet, theatre maker and host from Cornwall, living in
Bristol. He is a host at Satellite of Love, a co-producer of the queer
poetry special for Lyra Festival and was a Young Curator with MAYK for
Mayfest 2024.

His first poetry pamphlet, Saints of Golden Hour was released in
February 2023 which explores soberness, girlhood, queer relationships
and the gods we create for ourselves. He is currently collaborating on
the production of the spoken word theatre show, Girlhood in T which
explores transness, masculinity and friendship.

**Edson Burton**

Dr Edson Burton is a prolific writer of audio, live drama and poetry.

Edson won the 2025 Tinniswood Prize for Man Friday an adaption of
Daniel Defoe's Robinson Crusoe.

His previous audio dramas include the acclaimed R4 series Deacon
starring Don Warrington.

Recent live work includes the listening journey _Duppy Hunter_
produced by Tamasha Theatre, and the theatrical promenade Destination
Old Market

He is the author of the poetry collections, Seasoned and Witness.

He is a member of Writers Mosaic the film collective Come the
Revolution, a board member of Lyra poetry festival and Afrika Eye film
festival.

Back by popular demand: Summer Lates at Bristol Dockyards.

We're opening the gates after hours allowing you to step into the new SS Great Britain
Experience while the crowds have gone, before exploring the iconic ship. As the light
softens over the harbour, enjoy a tipple on the top deck, stay for a BBQ and live music
from Champagne Chateau in partnership with Diverse Artists Network.

dockside elegance and swing-jazz. In partnership with Diverse Artists Network.

to enjoy as the sun sets. The perfect accompaniment to live music, a glass of something
cold and the most spectacular backdrop.

Tickets must be booked online in advance and are non-refundable, though they can be
transferred to a new date up to 24 hours before, subject to availability. Your ticket
includes entry to SS Great Britain for the duration of the event only. Summer Lates will
go ahead in most weather conditions, and there is a wet weather option in place. Summer
lates are aimed at an adult audience but supervised children are welcome; anyone aged 18
or under must be accompanied by an adult. Smoking and vaping are prohibited everywhere on
site.

price.text: Admission is free; tickets are not required.

events.raw:
**Yokai: Japanese Spirits and Folklore** — Fri, 21 Aug 2026 – Wed, 26 Aug
2026. PV 6:00–9:00 pm; daily 10:00 am–4:00 pm.

Group exhibition presenting the work of animators, printmakers,
model-makers and illustrators, with artworks inspired by Yokai: ghosts,
monsters and spirits from traditional Japanese folklore.
events.summary: Eight artists — animators, printmakers, illustrators and model-makers — take on the ghosts, monsters and spirits of Japanese folklore, in sculpture, woodblock prints, paintings and drawings.
events.description:
*Yokai: Japanese Spirits and Folklore* is a group exhibition of work by
animators, printmakers, illustrators and model-makers all inspired by
the theme of Yokai, the ghosts, monsters and spirits from traditional
Japanese folklore.

Handmade sculptures, Japanese woodblock prints and original paintings
and drawings make up the exhibit, which is sponsored by Doublecat
Productions — an animation company based in Bristol and Tokyo.

**Dates:** Friday 21st August – Wednesday 26th August
**Private View / Opening Night:** Friday 21st of August, 6:00 pm – 9:00 pm
**Opening Hours:** Daily, 10:00 am – 4:00 pm

**Workshops and Events:** Drop-in Yokai Drawing Workshop, Saturday 22nd
August, 12 – 3 pm

**Participating Artists:** Aco Decodoll, Ben Spybey, Kiri
Horikiki-White, Laura Tofarides, Luke Hyde, Marta Dias, Martyna
Sabadasz, Seb Burnett

**Entry:** Admission is free; tickets are not required.

**Accessibility:** The exhibition space is fully wheelchair accessible,
with step-free entry and wide pathways throughout. An accessible toilet
is available on-site. Seating is provided within the exhibition for
visitors who may need to rest. Assistance dogs are welcome and staff
are available to offer support if needed.

events.description:
Join us at The Georgian House Museum for some Family Fun this summer!

This enchanting activity day will celebrate the literary excellence of Jane Austen with
something to do for all the family.

Upcoming 2026 dates: Friday 21 August, Saturday 22 August.

What's on:

- Immerse yourself in the world of Jane Austen
- Make your very own fan to take home with you!
- Get your face painted
- Join our friendly volunteers for historical story time
- Dress up in our historical costumes for both children and grown-ups
- Explore our historic museum and garden, trails are included in the price of the ticket
- Capture the experience with props and fanciful backdrops, be sure to tag your photos
  @bristolmuseums on Instagram!
- Enjoy some Georgian sights, sounds and smells!

Come ready to explore, learn, and make memories in the beautiful surroundings of The
Georgian House Museum.

Entry tickets are £5 per person (except children under 4) and activities are included
in the entry price. Discounted family group tickets are available. Walk ins on the day
if space is available.

**Summer 2026 VAT reduction** — We're taking part in the Government's summer VAT
reduction scheme. For you, this means lower prices tickets, and reductions on children's
meals at our cafés. VAT reductions for adult tickets are included on this event.

events.summary: A free facilitated space to sit with feelings about climate change alongside neighbours — no advice given, no action expected, and listening is enough.
events.description:
With the recent heatwaves many local people have been feeling the
impacts of climate change on their everyday life. Come together with
neighbours to reflect and share feelings about climate change in a
caring and considerate space.

Questions about the event can be emailed to: futuremancy@gmail.com

Not sure what a Climate Cafe is? We liked this quick explainer from
the Climate Psychology Alliance of North America:
https://www.climatepsychology.us/climate-cafes/.

This is a space that is designed for us to reflect on our feelings
about the changing climate, which can often be difficult to access.
As such, you don't have to do anything, and you won't be expected to
sign up to any action or activity, unless that feels supportive to
you. You can just listen. No-one will be giving advice, and no
emotional response is 'wrong'. We are not trying to minimise, change
or 'look on the bright side' of any reaction you might have. We are
expressing these feelings together.

events.title: Friendly Neighbourhood Film Club: In The Best Interests of Children
events.raw:
**Friendly Neighbourhood Film Club: In The Best Interests of
Children** — Saturday 22 August 2026, 12:00–14:00, £5. A
family-friendly screening of the 1977 documentary by Elizabeth
Stevens, Cathy Zheutlin and Frances Reid, presented with Reverie
Cineclub.
events.summary: A rarely screened 1977 documentary following lesbian mothers fighting for custody of their children, made to educate family court judges and now a landmark of queer family history — with tea and talk afterwards.
events.description:
Friendly Neighbourhood Film Club and Reverie Cineclub present a
family-friendly screening of IN THE BEST INTERESTS OF THE CHILDREN
(1977), the groundbreaking documentary by Elizabeth Stevens, Cathy
Zheutlin and Frances Reid following lesbian mothers fighting for the
right to custody of their children.

Rarely screened for many years, this remarkable and underseen
documentary offers an intimate portrait of eight families. Giving
equal space to mothers and their children, the film captures their
experiences of family, upbringing and queer parenthood with warmth
and raw honesty. Originally produced to educate family court judges,
it has since become an important document of LGBTQ+ family history
and feminist filmmaking.

Made at a time when lesbian mothers routinely lost custody of their
children because of their sexuality, the film documents the legal and
social challenges these families faced while centering their
experiences of love and community. Through candid interviews and
snapshots of everyday life, the film reveals both the realities of
discrimination, and the strength, dignity and joy of queer families.

We chose this film because of the care with which it approaches its
subjects. While some laws and societal attitudes have changed since
the film was made, LGBTQ+ people continue to face barriers and public
debate around family life and parenthood. IN THE BEST INTERESTS OF
THE CHILDREN remains a timely reminder of why these stories matter.

After the screening, there will be space to stay, chat and reflect
together over tea and coffee. Whether you're discovering the film for
the first time or revisiting this landmark of queer cinema, everyone
is welcome.

events.raw: **Event 24/08: Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi introduces The Ghost of the Mountains** — From £6.00.
events.summary: Conservation scientist Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi on twenty years tracking snow leopards in the high Himalaya, and the book that came out of it.
events.description:
**We are absolutely thrilled to welcome the award-winning scientist and conservationist, Dr Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi, to discuss his debut novel, *The Ghost of the Mountains: Unravelling the Secrets of the Snow Leopard*. The Ghost of the Mountains is a story of discovery, conservation and adventure on the trail of one of the most elusive and mysterious predators, brought to life by the world-leading expert on snow leopards.**

**Date:**
Monday 24th of August

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 19:00. Finish approx 20:00.

**Tickets:**
£6 ticket only
£20 ticket with *The Ghost of the Mountains* (hardback)

You don't need to bring your ticket with you, we will have a list of names on the door. Books will be available to buy on the night.

**ABOUT THE BOOK**

***The Ghost of the Mountain: Unravelling the Secrets of the Snow Leopard***

Silent, solitary and beautiful: snow leopards inhabit the cliffs and rugged mountains of central Asia at heights of over 3,000 metres. Thickly furred, with silver-grey pelts, they are so well camouflaged that they vanish into the rocky landscape.

For twenty years, scientist and mountaineer Dr Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi– known as Kullu– has studied the snow leopard in the highest reaches of the Himalaya. The snow leopard is the most elusive of cats.

With their silver-grey pelts and long tails, they move silently through glaciers, snow, rocks and the icy peaks of their wild, mountainous habitat. Rarely seen, they are often regarded as mythical, but this is an animal that faces extraordinary daily challenges, and whose survival depends on the delicate balance of climate, prey, landscape and local people.

Living for months at a time in some of the most difficult-to-reach places on earth, Kullu has pioneered research that shines fresh light on these charismatic and vulnerable animals. His work makes a compelling and urgent case for their conservation.

Combining scientific authority, high-altitude fieldwork and powerful storytelling, *The Ghost of the Mountains* is a gripping exploration into what it takes to save the snow leopard.

*‘A brave, unique field-study of the most extraordinary cat on the planet - the Snow*
*Leopard - elusive, Spartan and beautiful’ Desmond Morris*

*‘Enchanting. The author is a most amiable guide on the mountainside, and this deeply*
*informed book gave me hope for the future of conservation’ Sara Wheeler*

*'Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi has spent his adult life studying, following and trying to protect snow leopards. The Ghost of the Mountains takes readers into the field, high in the Himalayas. The story it tells is by turns beautiful, terrible, and encouraging’ Elizabeth Kolbert*

*‘What a thrilling and intrepid story. Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi takes us into the icy heights of the Himalaya, tracking the elusive snow leopard and bringing to life both this solitary animal and the threatened world it inhabits. Beautifully told, it's a tale of beauty, drama and wild landscapes but also one of the entangled lives of snow leopards, their prey and the humans who share their terrain’ Andrea Wulf*

*‘Marvellous - quite literally. A thrilling story of adventure amongst high mountains, deep mysteries, elusive animals and vertiginous facts’ Charles Foster*

***ABOUT THE AUTHOR***

**Dr Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi** is an award-winning scientist and conservationist who has studied the snow leopard for twenty years. A Fellow of the British Ecological Society, he is a scientist with the Nature Conservation Foundation, a National NGO in India, and the Country Director for the Snow Leopard Trust, an international NGO. His field research is concentrated in India, Nepal, Kyrgyzstan and Mongolia. *The Ghost of the Mountains* is his first book.

events.raw:
**Poetry Peace Feast** — Tuesday 25 August 2026, 19:00–21:00. £15
adults / £7.50 children, with "Pay it Forward" tickets. Bridges for
Communities present an evening of storytelling, conversation and
poetry with Bristol Poet Laureate Sukina Noor and restorative poet
Leeza Awojobi.
events.summary: Bridges for Communities bring their peace feast back to the Folk House — a shared meal with Bristol Poet Laureate Sukina Noor and Leeza Awojobi, built around the question of how you sustain a village.
events.description:
We're returning to Bristol Folk House! Join us for an evening of
storytelling, conversation and poetry featuring Bristol Poet Laureate
Sukina Noor and restorative poet Leeza Awojobi. This is invitation to
share in food which nourishes the body and soul, exchange meaningful
ideas and leave feeling energised for the wellbeing of your community.

At Bridges for Communities, we love all things collective and have
recently been thinking about the phrase 'It takes a Village'. We know
it takes a village, but how to sustain one? This peace feast builds on
a conversation we've been having in a more creative way. It explores
the complex tension between the needs of the individual and the
collective. It brings together storytelling and collaboration in a way
which suggests rather than dictates, opening up fresh pathways for
engaging across difference. For those feeling extra bold, come
prepared to share your thoughts in an informal guided activity.

Peace Feasts bring people together around a meal, to listen to music,
exchange stories and hear from guest speakers. They celebrate local
communities, help us to see the world through someone else's eyes, and
create spaces for friendships to grow between people from different
backgrounds and experiences of life.

events.title: Introduction to Conservation (3-day course) for 16-30 yr olds
events.ageRestriction: 16–30 year olds; anyone under 18 must have parental consent to attend.
events.raw:
**Introduction to Conservation (3-day course) for 16-30 yr olds**

Wednesday 26 August 2026 – Friday 28 August 2026, 10:00am - 2:30pm. Grow
Wilder, Bristol.

"Do you want to get into conservation, learn more about nature and wildlife or
meet like-minded people?"
events.summary:
Three days behind the scenes at Avon Wildlife Trust for 16- to 30-year-olds:
habitat management and practical tasks, then ecology and wildlife monitoring,
then communication, advocacy and careers advice.
events.description:
A 3-day course offering young people behind-the-scenes experience at Avon
Wildlife Trust, covering wildlife conservation and land management. It provides
foundational knowledge in conservation work, practical fieldwork skills, and
insight into the various roles at the charity.

Day 1 focuses on land and habitat management, including practical conservation
tasks, discussions on sustainable practices, and horticultural work.

Day 2 covers ecology and wildlife monitoring through techniques like moth
trapping, mammal tracking, pond dipping, bird transects and owl pellet
dissection.

Day 3 addresses communication, education and advocacy within conservation, plus
wellbeing activities and career guidance.

For 16-30-year-olds. Anyone under 18 must have parental consent to attend.
Grow Wilder, 181 Frenchay Park Road, Bristol, BS16 1EL (what3words
frog.tested.tidy). Booking through the Eventbrite widget on the event page.

events.summary: August's translated fiction club takes Rene Karabash's She Who Remains, shortlisted for the 2026 International Booker and translated from Bulgarian by Izidora Angel.
events.description:
**Join us for an exciting evening to discuss translated literature. Whether you're a fan of literary fiction or just looking to try something new, this book club hopes to achieve just that. In August, we will be looking at Rene Karabash's She Who Remains, translated from Bulgarian by Izidora Angel, which was shortlisted for the 2026 International Booker Prize.**

***Date:***

Thursday 28th of August

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**
Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *SHE WHO REMAINS***

High in the Accursed Mountains, in a village ruled by the ancient laws of the Kanun, Bekija escapes an arranged marriage by becoming a sworn virgin, renouncing her womanhood to live as a man.

Her decision sets off a brutal chain of events, destroying her family and separating her from the one she loves the most.

Years later, as Bekija – now Matija – tells their story to a visiting journalist, long-buried truths come to light, along with the realisation of all that might have been.

***Shortlisted for the 2026 International Booker Prize.***

**ABOUT *PEIRENE PRESS***

Peirene Press is an award-winning independent publisher. Founded in 2008, specialising in bringing exciting literary fiction and novellas from around the world, especially Europe, to English-language readers.

https://www.peirenepress.com/

events.title: Forwards Festival 2026
events.raw:
**FORWARDS RETURNS FOR 2026** — "A Music Festival in Bristol, For The
Future".

"FORWARDS: an inner city music festival drawing the biggest names in
international music to Bristol Downs."

Two days, Saturday 29 and Sunday 30 August, with the lineup published A-Z
by day and no set times. [Buy
tickets](https://www.forwardsbristol.co.uk/buyticketsaxs) via AXS.
events.summary: The two-day music festival on the Downs, headlined this year by Tems, Maribou State and Self Esteem on the Saturday and Little Simz, Amyl and The Sniffers and Dijon on the Sunday, with a kids area, food and drink and The Information stage of talks alongside the music.
events.description:
FORWARDS: an inner city music festival drawing the biggest names in
international music to Bristol Downs. The festival aims to present high
quality, diverse and heritage music acts alongside emerging artists from
Bristol & beyond.

The festival presents a contemporary curation of music while paying homage
to Bristol's long standing history of being a music city. In addition,
FORWARDS is more than just a music festival, it looks to challenge what
metropolitan festivals can be today and how they can do good, from the
inside out. The 2-day festival aims to harness the power of live events to
bring people together for incredible music moments and lasting positive
change.

At the heart of the festival is FORWARDS THINKING, a platform for year round
social initiatives in Bristol, all through our partners, Big Team CIC and
Team Canteen CIC. Alongside these partners is The Information, a dedicated
space at FORWARDS for debate and understanding on today's current affairs
and cultural issues.

events.description:
Visit Kings Weston Roman Villa and find out about this fascinating archaeological site.

Explore where Romans used to live right on Bristol's doorstep and discover the remains
of a real Roman villa complete with mosaic floors, underfloor heating systems and a
bath suite.

There's plenty of family fun to enjoy too with craft, dressing up, trails and more.

Kings Weston Roman Villa is open regularly throughout the summer season. Upcoming 2026
open days: Saturday 29 August, Saturday 26 September. Join us from 10am to 2pm.

Free, donations welcome. This is a drop in event, no booking required. Kings Weston
Roman Villa is an outdoor archaeological site with some uneven surfaces, grassy areas
and low walls. Parking is available in the residential streets that surround the
villa. Buses 3 or 4 stop on the Long Cross.

- Join our friendly volunteers for story time
- Join in with Tudor crafts, make your very own headdress and Tudor jewels to take home

- Get your face painted
- Dress up in our historical costumes for both children and grown-ups
- Explore our historic museum and garden, trails are included in the price of the ticket

events.summary: Riddlestick Theatre's new folk-theatre piece, set among a company of wartime runaways hiding in the Cornish cliffs, with live music and a 75-minute running time.
events.description:
An enchanting tale of ritual magic and misfortune set by the sea in 1917 – a brand-new show from acclaimed folk theatre company Riddlestick Theatre (*Barleycorn*, *The Cabinet of Madame Fanny Du Thé*)

Lizard Point, 1917. While the war grinds on in France, the mysterious Crow and his company of runaways spend their days in a fever of conjured dreams. In their refuge amongst the cliffs, hidden away from the prying eyes of the police, the troupe rejoice in strange rituals and tales of long-lost loves.

But the tides are turning. Crow has taken to watching the sea. The voices of the dead are getting louder. And when a soldier from the front line washes up on the rocks nearby, the truth about Crow, and Lizard Point, threatens to drown them all.

A brand-new show from acclaimed folk theatre company Riddlestick Theatre, conjuring a darkly comic blend of occult intrigue and enchanting live music.

**Performances:** Sun 30th August at 7:00 pm, Mon 31st August at 7:30 pm, Tue 1st September at 7:30 pm. Tickets £14. Running time 75 mins (no interval). Suitable for ages 12+.

**Whether you’re a fan of the series or looking to delve into romance fiction, our Romance book club offers a joyful escape. We're building a community to gush over swoon-worthy characters and a safe space to discuss themes like relationships. With *ACOTAR 6* coming out this Autumn, our Romance Book Club is reading through the entire series in anticipation of its release. **

**ABOUT *A COURT OF WINGS AND RUIN (BOOK THREE)***

Feyre has returned to the Spring Court, determined to gather information on Tamlin's manoeuvrings and the invading king threatening to bring her land to its knees. But to do so she must play a deadly game of deceit – and one slip may spell doom not only for Feyre, but for her world as well.

As war bears down upon them all, Feyre must decide who to trust amongst the dazzling and lethal High Lords and hunt for allies in unexpected places. And her heart will face the ultimate test as she and her mate are forced to question whether they can truly trust each other.

**ABOUT *A COURT OF FROST AND STARLIGHT (BOOK FOUR)***

In this companion tale to the bestselling *A Court of Thorns and Roses** series*, Feyre, Rhys and their friends are working to rebuild the Night Court and the vastly changed world beyond after the events of *A Court of Wings and Ruin*.

But Winter Solstice is finally near, and with it a hard-earned reprieve. Yet even the festive atmosphere can't keep the shadows of the past from looming. As Feyre navigates her first Winter Solstice as High Lady, she finds that those dearest to her have more wounds than she anticipated – scars that will have a far-reaching impact on the future of their court.

***ABOUT SARAH J. MAAS***

Artist Niki Groom will be transforming Centrespace Gallery into a giant

walls, resulting in a colourful display of community.
events.summary: Ten years of Niki Groom's reportage illustration, from the Calais 'Jungle' to Bristol festivals and protests, hung as if the gallery were one large sketchbook. Free, with a sketching table and talks alongside.
events.description:
For this exhibition, artist Niki Groom will be transforming Centrespace
Gallery into a giant sketchbook. The walls will carry the illustrated
stories of people she's met — life-size paintings of dancers and
musicians, and a celebration of events that bring people together, such
as festivals, protests, sport and food.

Groom has specialised in reportage illustration for the humanitarian
and cultural sectors since 2016, when she documented the Calais
'Jungle' for Choose Love — creating impactful imagery that allows
people to remain anonymous. She has worked with local organisations
including Refugee Women of Bristol and Bristol Refugee Festival.

The exhibition includes workshops, talks on creativity and community, a
sketching table, and merchandise featuring original artwork.

**Dates:** Tuesday 1 September 11:00 – Tuesday 8 September 2026 18:00
**Private View:** Friday 4th September, 6:00 – 9:00 pm
**Opening Hours:** Daily, 11:00 am – 6:00 pm
**Entry:** Admission is free; tickets are not required.

events.description:
*'Man overboard, man overboard! Call control. Blow the whistle.'*

Love is a complicated business. It gets even more complicated when the person you love doesn't want to be alive. Tender, funny and defiantly hopeful, *The Light House* is a real-life story of falling in love and staying in love, even when the lights go out and you're lost in the dark. Join the emergency response as we dance in the kitchen, sing in the streets and try to turn the lights back on. It gets lonely, muddling through these days and nights. So why don't we do it together?

*The Light House* is the highly acclaimed debut play of theatre artist, Aly Williams.

**Date:** Wednesday, 2nd September 2026, 7:30pm. Tickets £14. Running time 1 hour (no interval). Suitable for ages 12+.

**Content warnings:** References to depression, suicide/suicidal ideation and hospitalisation.

events.summary: A free online orientation for UWE's eight-week Mindful Eating course, including a short guided practice. Open to anyone over 18.
events.description:
Mindful Eating - Conscious Living is an eight-week mindfulness programme
that will help you to establish a regular mindfulness practice, and help
you to make better choices to manage your mood and stress levels.

The focus will be around learning how to be less anxious and more at
ease around food and eating. By practicing paying attention to the
present moment, without judgement, we can cultivate the capacity to tune
into the physical experience of eating and how they relate to our moods
and emotions. In time, we can regain our natural freedom around food.

This short course is appropriate for anyone over the age of 18 who is
interested in mindfulness meditation or mindful eating. You need to be
willing to practise the in-class exercises at home between sessions, to
fully benefit from the programme.

**Registration and tickets.** The orientation session is a chance to find
out more about the course and ask any questions you may have. It will
also be an opportunity for you to experience a short practice in a small
group environment, which can help you to assess whether this course is
right for you at this time. Upon completion of your orientation session,
you will be invited to formally register on the course and pay your
course fees via the UWE Bristol WPM System. Attendance at the orientation
session is a course requirement.

Cost: Free. Attendance: booking required. This is an online event on
Microsoft Teams.

events.title: Kaleidoscope Fusion – Dance Night
events.raw: **Kaleidoscope Fusion – Dance Night** — Sep 5, 19:30–23:00. £5.
events.summary: A fusion social dance party — partner dancing without the baggage — opening with an all-levels intro workshop and running into DJ sets. No partner or experience needed; sliding-scale entry.
events.description:
We throw dance parties where all bodies are invited. You already know
how to dance, we're just here to give you permission to embrace all of
the ways your body wants to move.

The evening opens with an all-levels workshop at 7:45pm, with local
teachers offering an intro to social dancing, followed by DJs playing
tracks ranging from slow and squishy to high-energy bangers. No partner
or prior experience is necessary.

One core principle: be excellent to one another — respect boundaries
and consent. Fusion is partner dancing, without the baggage, fusing
various dance styles through improvisation. The organisers note their
approach is queer, it is feminist, and they don't want anyone left
behind.

The single-level venue provides accessible entry from pavement to
dancefloor, with modifications available on request.

Sliding scale: £5 (low income), £10 (general release), £15
(pay-it-forward). Tickets via hdfst.uk/kaleidoscope-fusion.

## Stand Up For The Weekend with Andrew Bird Featuring Javier Jarquin & compere Ross Smith

#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly show from The Comedy Box featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: ANDREW BIRD

Andrew Bird is a top headline act throughout the UK and Ireland and has performed all around the world. He is highly in demand as a tour support for big name comics such as Rhod Gilbert, Rob Brydon, Jon Richardson and Michael McIntyre playing venues such as Wembley and O2 arenas, and is one of the hardest working TV warm-up acts in the industry having worked on shows as varied as Pointless, Have I Got News For You, The Jonathan Ross Show and Taskmaster.

There is a very good reason for Andrew Bird’s popularity. He is always funny and frequently hilarious. He’s a nimble storyteller, with a relaxed, personable style. He simply proves cracking company, whether he’s got an angle or not. Fast, fluid and animated, you might mistake his relentless chatter for a spontaneous stream of consciousness, were it not so effortlessly reliable in generating laughs.

#### “*A great storyteller, funny, likeable and effortless*” Time Out

#### “*Comedy gold…Bird’s going to be a big star, catch him close-up now*” The Scotsman

events.raw:
**Free mindful eating information session** — Mon 07 September 2026, 10:30
- 12:00, online: Microsoft Teams. Free, booking required. A free session
explaining mindfulness and mindful eating, and what the Mindful Eating -
Conscious Living programme entails.
events.summary: The second, morning orientation session for UWE's Mindful Eating course, online and free to attend.
events.description:
Mindful Eating - Conscious Living is an eight-week mindfulness programme
that will help you to establish a regular mindfulness practice, and help
you to make better choices to manage your mood and stress levels.

The focus will be around learning how to be less anxious and more at
ease around food and eating. By practicing paying attention to the
present moment, without judgement, we can cultivate the capacity to tune
into the physical experience of eating and how it relates to our moods
and emotions. In time we can regain our natural freedom around food.

This short course is appropriate for anyone over the age of 18 who is
interested in mindfulness meditation or mindful eating. You need to be
willing to practise the in-class exercises at home between sessions, to
fully benefit from the programme.

**Registration and tickets.** If you are interested in this course, you
will be invited to attend an orientation session. The orientation session
is a chance to find out more about the course and ask any questions you
may have. It will also be an opportunity for you to experience a short
practice in a small group environment, which can help you to assess
whether this course is right for you at this time. On completion of your
orientation session, you will be invited to formally register on the
course and pay your course fees via the UWE Bristol WPM System.
Attendance at the orientation session is a course requirement.

Cost: Free. Attendance: booking required. This is an online event on
Microsoft Teams.

events.description:
Relax, re-balance mind & body in a heart-opening, healing Sound Bath with breath taking
views of Bristol's iconic suspension bridge.

Join the experience led by Rounik Sound Healing at Clifton Observatory. Participants
will find themselves in a tranquil and grounding setting of soothing candles,
glimmering fairy-lights, and the serene sounds of gongs, singing bowls and sacred
chimes.

The session includes a journey of relaxation, guided meditation and sound therapy.
Spaces are limited; attendees should bring yoga mats and blankets.

Sound healing offers a relaxing and re-tuning experience that assists our brain to
enter deeper, slower states and encourages physical repair on a cellular level. The
practice supports emotional processing and life transitions.

The session begins with a check-in and intention-setting, followed by breathwork for
connection to ourselves, and a chakra balancing guided meditation, before the sound
bath begins.

**What to bring:** yoga mat, water bottle, blankets, and cushions for comfort.

**Contraindications:** not recommended for those with extreme sound sensitivity,
epilepsy, or first-trimester pregnancy.

This introductory woodworking course teaches students to create a
softwood toolbox with a handle and inset base using traditional hand
tools and corner rebate joints. Upon completion, participants take

home projects or advance to Level 2 classes.

- Sawing straight and square
- Accurately marking out and cutting joints
- Effectively using hand tools including chisels and planes
- Fitting and finishing woodwork projects

events.summary: Two halves of unscripted comedy in the Chicken Shed: audience-prompted improv games hosted by Ste Brown, then two-prov duo Birdwatchers.
events.description:
Wednesday Night Improv returns to the Hen & Chicken with two halves of unscripted comedy – all made up on the spot, all inspired by your suggestions. Expect quick wit, bold characters, and the kind of laughter that only happens when nobody knows what’s coming next (including the performers).

**## FIRST HALF ##Comedy Games, Improvised Live**

*(Think Whose Line Is It Anyway? meets Game Changer, with a sprinkling of Taskmaster.)*

A fast, funny first half built around short improvised games – the kind where performers get a prompt from the audience and have seconds to turn it into something brilliant. Points will be awarded. Consequences may follow.

Featuring a brand new cast for a new season! TBA

And your host, Ste Brown.

**## SECOND HALF ##BIRDWATCHERS**

Birdwatchers are a two-prov team made up of Anna Kemp (This is Your Musical) and Paige Tummons (Jazz Police). In their original “epilogue” format, Birdwatchers explore the present and past of 2 characters reminiscing together. The exploratory flashbacks combine comedic elements, heartfelt scenes, and absolutely ridiculous moments that are sure to make you laugh and think that maybe your own family isn’t that weird after all.

Birdwatchers have performed extensively in Bristol and won the Improv Cagematch in 2019.

—

Whether you’re a seasoned comedy fan or just curious about what happens when performers make it all up as they go, this is a perfect night to dive into Bristol’s thriving improv scene. Expect laughter, surprises, and something completely different — every single time.

#### EXTRA DATE DUE TO POPULAR DEMAND

Podcasting cult hero.

Following his record-breaking Waterslide tour, Jamie Hutchinson is back with Can My Mate Come? He’s Sound. — a brand-new hour of unfiltered mayhem, questionable logic and emotional chaos held together by takeaway boxes and blind optimism.

Waterslide was a “masterclass in self-caricature” (British Comedy Guide). Now Jamie returns. Older? Technically. Less hair? Absolutely. Wiser? Absolutely not.

Armed with a bottomless pit of mad stories, misjudged decisions, and a unique ability for making the absurd feel profound, Jamie delivers what the British Comedy Guide called “rapid-fire gag-darts”.

Whether you’re a fan or just here because someone said “He’s Sound!” – good luck. You’re on his night out now.

**Age Guidance: 18+**

**Everyone is welcome at our Contemporary Fiction book club, where on the first Wednesday of every month we discuss a recently-published paperback novel. In September, we'll be delving into *The Correspondent *by Virginia Evans, winner of the 2026 Women's Prize of Fiction. **

***Date:*
Wednesday 9th of September

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**

Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *The Correspondent***

***Winner of the 2026 Women's Prize of Fiction***

Every morning, Sybil Van Antwerp sits down to write letters – to her brother, to her best friend, to the president of the university who will not allow her to attend a class she desperately wants to take, to her favourite authors to tell them what she thinks of their latest books, and to one person to whom she writes often yet never sends the letter. Because at seventy-three, Sybil has used her correspondence – witty and wise – to make sense of the world.

But beyond the page, she has spent the last thirty years keeping the people who love her at arms’ length... Until letters from someone in her past force her to examine one of the most painful periods of her life. Now, Sybil must send the letter she has been writing for all these years - and find forgiveness within herself in order to move on.

Sybil Van Antwerp’s life of letters might not be an extraordinary one, but she also might be one of the most memorable characters you will ever read.

events.description:
Get ready to build your yoga foundation in this 6-week course that
will leave you feeling centered and strong.

Yoga Foundations — 6-Week Beginners Course (formerly Yoga for
Beginners at Yogasara)

- St Anne's House, BS4
- Wednesdays, 6.00–7.00pm
- 9 September – 14 October

**What this course is about**

This 6-week course offers a gentle, supportive introduction to yoga.
We'll explore the four core elements of practice:

- Breathwork, to calm and steady the nervous system
- Meditation, simple practices for presence and perspective
- Asana (movement), building strength, steadiness and mobility
- Yoga philosophy, practical ideas you can take into everyday life

You don't need any experience, and you don't need to be flexible.
This isn't about achieving shapes, it's about learning how to work
with your body, your breath and your attention in a way that actually
supports real life.

**How the course is structured, and why**

This course runs several times a year, by design.

We learn together over six weeks, then there is space between courses
to integrate. Time to practise at home, attend regular classes with
new understanding, and notice what changes when you live with the
practices rather than rushing on to the next thing.

This is how learning really sticks.

When we repeat a practice, pause, and then return to it, the brain
lays down stronger neural pathways. Things that felt abstract start
to make sense in the body. You hear familiar instructions
differently. You move and breathe from a more informed, embodied
place.

Each time you return, you're not starting again, you're building on
lived experience.

**Saturday morning workshops, between courses**

In the spaces between the 6-week courses, I also offer Saturday
morning workshops for those who'd like to go a little deeper.

events.description:
Bristol's legendary, bold, endlessly inventive and genre-defying theatre company, Action Hero (*The Talent*, *Oh Europa*, *Watch Me Fall*) return with something brand new: Lost inside a recurring nightmare, a reluctant actor returns to the stage after 8 years to conquer his stage fright and banish his ghosts, but he's not gonna make a big song and dance about it.

Lost inside a recurring nightmare, a reluctant actor returns to the stage. In an attempt to conquer an 8-year period of intense stage fright – and inside a dream-world inhabited by the phantoms of his disapproving ancestors – he is replaying his own autobiography and starting to lose the plot. But he's not gonna make a big song and dance about it. Instead, he's determined to keep the show on the road, re-writing his anxiety dreams live on stage in the hope of banishing the ghosts of performances past.

*A Song & Dance* is an absurdist nightmare of a performance about masking, performing and 'acting the part'.
