events.title: Reds - Paul Mason on the Past, Present and Future of Communism

price.text: £30 includes a copy of the book; £6 general admission

events.raw:
**Reds - Paul Mason on the Past, Present and Future of Communism** — Friday 11th September 19:00, Waterstones, Bristol - Galleries.
A major analysis as we head into a dangerous new world order where China and Russia threaten major change to the world's democracies
events.summary: Paul Mason on Reds, his global history of communism, in conversation with Andrew Kelly, formerly of Bristol Ideas.
events.description:
It starts in antiquity, not in 1917. It centres not just on the obvious leaders and thinkers but asks how the idealism of millions of working-class activists could lead to their acquiescence in mass murder, repression and social atomisation. A fact whose legacy – unfortunately – is alive and kicking in both Russia and China today.

**Paul Mason**’s startling new book will argue that the desire to live without hierarchy and property is an impulse deeply rooted in our human nature. Reds traces the history of communist ideas through revolts in the ancient and medieval worlds, and chronicles the rise of 19th century anti-capitalist movements. Using first hand testimonies of both the perpetrators and the victims, Mason gives a new and terrifying account of how the 20th century experiment in communism turned into a totalitarian nightmare.

But, he argues, the story is not over. Western democracies are stagnant and lacking self-belief. Looming climate chaos demands radical economic answers. Millions of people in the global south see China’s offer of authoritarian, state-led development model as a viable alternative. And among the Western left, new forms of techno-egalitarianism vie with right-wing libertarianism in the battle over the digital future.

**Paul Mason** is a British journalist, author, broadcaster, and political commentator known for his economic and political analysis. Formerly Economics Editor at* BBC Newsnight* and *Channel 4 News*, he has written for *The New European*, *Social Europe*, and *Frankfurter Rundschau*, authored books like *Postcapitalism* and *How to Stop Fascism*, produced award-winning documentaries, and is active in progressive politics and defence policy.
He will be in conversation with **Andrew Kelly**, formerly director of* Bristol Ideas*.

Did you know there are 18 different species of bat in the UK? Did you know they
are the only true flying mammals in the world? Join us for an evening walk
through Grow Wilder and across to Stoke Park to see these great creatures in
action.

The event involves discussion of bat habitats, yearly cycles and conservation
needs, along with use of bat detectors to identify the species observed during
the walk. No prior expertise is required.

Participants should prepare for outdoor conditions with sturdy shoes,
appropriate clothing and a torch, as the return journey will occur in darkness
over uneven terrain.

This event is part of our Youth Programme so we ask anyone attending to be
between 14-25 years old. Anyone under 18 must have parental consent to attend.
Parents and siblings are also welcome. Meet at Grow Wilder, 181 Frenchay Park
Road, Bristol, BS16 1EL.

events.description:
**Whodunnit? Let's find out together! Our Crime and Thriller Book Club is built for readers who love the thrill of a good chase. Whether you're a lifelong fan of golden-age whodunnits or looking to dive into the genre for the first time, our goal is to create a welcoming, lively space to share theories, analyse motives, and celebrate great storytelling. Each month, we'll gather in person to dissect everything from the atmospheric pacing of classic thrillers to the complex puzzles of modern murder mysteries. **

**In September, we will be discussing *The Big Sleep *by Raymond Chandler: a classic noir that follows a cynical private investigator, Philip Marlowe.**

**Date:**
Monday 14th of September

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**
Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *THE BIG SLEEP***

Los Angeles PI Philip Marlowe is working for the Sternwood family.

Old man Sternwood, crippled and wheelchair-bound, is being given the squeeze by a blackmailer, and he wants Marlowe to make the problem go away. But with Sternwood's two wild, devil-may-care daughters prowling LA's seedy backstreets, Marlowe's got his work cut out, and that's before he stumbles over the first corpse...

*The Big Sleep* is Raymond Chandler's first novel featuring laconic PI Philip Marlowe.

***ABOUT RAYMOND CHANDLER***

Raymond Thornton Chandler was born in Chicago in 1888, but moved to England with his family when he was twelve, where he attended Dulwich College, alma mater to some of the twentieth century's most renowned writers. Returning to America in 1912, he settled in California, worked in a number of jobs, and later married.

It was during the Depression era that he seriously turned his hand to writing, and his first published story appeared in the pulp magazine *Black Mask* in 1933, followed six years later, when he was fifty, by his first novel, *The Big Sleep.*

Chandler died in 1959, having established himself as the finest crime writer in America.

*Storysmith, 236 North Street, Bristol, BS3 1JD ([click here for a map](https://maps.app.goo.gl/9N9dxXfnwxac83FY7))*

We are stoked to welcome a truly singular literary talent to Bristol in September: **Tice Cin** will be with us to discuss her second novel **Safe Spaces**!

As longtime fans of Cin’s debut novel Keeping The House, we are especially excited to be hosting – expect an enlivening and perspective-altering chat about a book which is already gathering incredible praise. Tice will be in conversation with **Ralf Webb**.

***Pre-order your copy of Safe Spaces** (rrp £14.99) for a special discounted price with your ticket, then collect on the night!*

## About Tice Cin

**Tice Cin** is an interdisciplinary artist and author from North London. Her debut novel **Keeping the House** (2021) received a Somerset Maugham Award and a London Writers Award, was a Guardian Book of the Year and was shortlisted for a British Book Award and the Desmond Elliot Prize among other accolades. Its accompanying mixtape having her named as one of Notion Magazines Ones to Watch. Her BBC Radio 4 documentary How Much Can You Say? (2024) won an Audio Production Award. Her work has been published and commissioned by Granta Magazine, London Magazine, Somerset House, Montblanc, Cartier and more. She is the founder of the interdisciplinary production company Neoprene Genie. Cin’s sophomore novel **Safe Spaces** will be published by Granta in September 2026. Cin lives between North London and North Cyprus.

*Photo credit: Eric Aydin Barberini*

## About Safe Spaces

Our unnamed narrator survives in London on a combination of Universal Credit, music production and songwriting, trying to figure out what she wants from the city, and whether the city is prepared to give it to her. Navigating love affairs and blinded by grief following the death of her closest confidante, Safe Spaces is a portrait of the artist as a young musician. Of the DJ booths, green rooms and dance floors that shape her, and the worlds she finds herself in: be they the grime and electronic nightclubs, her Turkish-Cypriot family, the beauty parlour, the studio.

At once a songbook, a collection of aphorisms, a therapy transcript and a community journal, Safe Spaces is a work of extraordinary lyricism and candour, confirming Tice Cin as one of the foremost stylists of her generation. An intimate portrait of a community and a moving personal reckoning, it fearlessly asks: can the dream of a safe space ever be realised?

*“Being able to capture so much raw emotion through incredible writing like this is a gift. This book conveys magical and visceral energy, that everyone should have the luxury of experiencing. Powerful shit”* – Lola Young

*“Safe Spaces makes a universe of London in all its glory, cruelty, poetry and bureaucracy. This is a book that evokes the shattering effect of trauma on prose, then painstakingly reconstructs a way to experience life, and talk about love. I saw in it a feat of outstanding energy to keep looking, keep listening and, feel everything in a time of grief, and yet somehow overstate nothing.” – *Amber Hussain

*“At first discordant, finally symphonic, Cin captures the heavy beat of her city’s blood, its healing music, in ways that recall and update the vivid prose-poetry of Clarence Major and Elizabeth Smart. This is an honest, intimate, grief-soaked work of experiential wonder.” – *Tom Benn, author of Oxblood

*“With arresting street smarts and vulnerability, Tice Cin reshapes London literature to ends previously unknown. We should all be grateful.” *– Matthew Sperling

events.title: In Conversation: Pete Wharmby & Lisa Galley
events.raw:
**In Conversation: Pete Wharmby & Lisa Galley** — Tuesday 15th September 19:00, Waterstones, Bristol - Galleries.
How can we really help autistic children in education?
events.summary: Two writers on supporting autistic children — Pete Wharmby on school systems, Lisa Galley on parenting — with questions and signing after.
events.description:
We're delighted to host **Pete Wharmby** and** Lisa Galley** for a discussion on education and care for autistic children.

In *Different Minds*, neurodivergence campaigner Pete Wharmby shines a light on what it's like to be autistic in Western school systems today, so we can understand how to support our children through the most important years of their lives.

With gentle science, practical tools and deep validation, Lisa Galley's *Parenting your Autistic Child* explains exactly what is happening in your child's brain and body during these difficult moments – when they refuse to get dressed, experience sensory overload or meltdown at 3.30pm – offering practical strategies that work with their nervous system rather than against it.

This informative and compassionate talk will be your chance to learn more, ask questions and get copies of the books signed.

**Peter Wharmby** is a neurodivergence campaigner and former teacher who was diagnosed autistic at age 34. He is also father to an autistic child. Shocked by the statistics around depression, anxiety and life expectancy for autistic people, Pete has immersed himself in working to improve neurodiversity awareness, acceptance and making the world a more suitable place for the neurodivergent community to live in.

**Lisa Galley** is an Autism Family Consultant, and former Speech and Language Therapist. She is also a dedicated mum to grown-up autistic kids. Her mission is to empower parents of neurodivergent children to reject the unrealistic neurotypical expectations that society places on autistic children, and to embrace intuitive parenting that aligns with the unique needs of their amazing kids.

Celebrate over 50 years of Pink Floyd's legendary album The Dark Side of the Moon with a new

Set to the newly remastered audio by James Guthrie and Joel Plante of das boot recording,
the sound is richer, deeper, and more powerful than ever. The breath-taking 360° visuals,

He was the special guest of friend Jim Jefferies for his Hammersmith Apollo dates in London. He is also a founder member of Altitude Comedy Festival, staged in the Alps. Andrew has recorded three Live DVDs with 2Entertain (Conflict Revolution, Andrew Maxwell: Live In Dublin & Andrew Maxwell: One Inch Punch).

(ITV) Celebrity Juice (ITV2) and Mock The Week (BBC Two). He is also the voice of Get Your Tats Out: Kavos Inc (Channel 5). Winner of King of Comedy.​

events.description:
This event is hosted by our partners at Intelligence Squared.

American democracy is on the brink. Masked agents menace the streets of Minneapolis. Donald Trump jokes about cancelling elections. And traditional allies like Canada and the UK are beginning to look for alliances that could replace their pivotal relationships with the US.

According to** Anthony Scaramucci**, former White House Communications Director turned outspoken Trump critic and host of the Rest is Politics: U.S., President Trump represents one of the most serious challenges the country has faced.

This autumn, on the eve of the pivotal US midterm elections, Scaramucci comes to live audiences across the UK to offer an insider’s account of how America reached this moment and to offer a hopeful message for how it might find a way back. Drawing on his forthcoming book *All The Wrong Moves*, he will trace a series of catastrophic decisions made by both Democrats and Republicans that in Scaramucci’s view dismantled decades of postwar stability and prosperity. And he will describe how undoing these mistakes can unlock a new era of success for America and the world.

Don’t miss this opportunity to see Anthony Scaramucci – hilarious, irreverent, insightful and deeply sourced within both the Republican and Democratic parties – live in-person and ask your own questions in the audience Q&A.

events.description:
Littleton Warth offers a wide expanse of grazed saltmarsh, with fine views
across to the Forest of Dean and down to the Severn Bridge, and a remote,
untamed atmosphere.

Expect the common saltmarsh plants in September, with particular focus on the
site's notably large population of Slender Hare's-ear (*Bupleurum
tenuissimum*), an anomalous and nationally scarce member of the carrot family.
Sea Clover (*Trifolium squamosum*), Strawberry Clover (*Trifolium fragiferum*)
and potentially Bulbous Foxtail (*Alopecurus bulbosus*) are also mentioned, and
the seawall supports grassland plants.

2:30pm start. Leader: David Hawkins. Meet at the car park at the end of Whale
Wharf Lane, ST588910, ///clincher.alive.begun, nearest postcode BS35 1NP.

**Home Education Day** — Meet real-life engineers, enjoy hands-on STEM activities, and

events.summary: The whole site opened for home-educating families only, with Babcock and dockyard engineers on hand and three bookable extras — a ship tour and two workshops.
events.description:
Bristol Dockyards is home to the remarkable legacy of Victorian engineer Isambard Kingdom
Brunel, but engineering is far from history. Join us this autumn for a special Home
Education Day where you can meet real-life engineers from Babcock and Bristol Dockyards,
discover what they do, and take part in hands-on STEM activities. You'll also have the
chance to learn more about Brunel and explore our newly opened museum dedicated to his
most famous ship, the SS Great Britain.

**What's included:** whole site access including the Brunel Institute, Being Brunel
Museum, SS Great Britain & NEW museum and Historic Dockyards.

**Key info** — Price: £9.00 pp; free for children 3 and under and carers accompanying a
paying disabled person. Date & time: Monday 21st September 2026, 10am-3pm.

**Additional bookable activities:**

- **Guided Tour of SS Great Britain** — Find out about the SS Great Britain's long and
  adventurous life, discover passengers and crew stories as you explore the ship with our
  knowledgeable volunteer tour guides. 10:30-11:30, 60 mins, on board the ship, meeting at
  the stern. £2 per child, adults free but must be booked in.
- **Brunel's Big Ideas** (education workshop) — Take a closer look at some of Brunel's
  sketches, discover how the SS Great Britain was built then hunt for some of Brunel's
  engineering tools in one of our museums. 10:30-11:30, 60 mins, Medlock classroom, Dry
  Dock and Being Brunel Museum. For children working at Key Stage 1 or 2. £3 per
  participating child, £1 per non-participating child, adults free.
- **Mission: Save the Ship** (education workshop) — Investigate the dehumidification system

events.summary: Patricia Lockwood in the shop for the first time, marking her new poetry collection Agate Head / Stone Soup and talking about whatever else comes up.
events.description:
*Storysmith, 236 North Street, Bristol, BS3 1JD ([click here for a map](https://maps.app.goo.gl/9N9dxXfnwxac83FY7))*

Join us as we welcome a Storysmith all-time favourite, live in the shop for the very first time! The one and only **Patricia Lockwood**, the original Priestdaughter, will be in Bristol to mark the release of her new poetry collection, **Agate Head / Stone Soup**, and in conversation about this alongside other matters.

You may know Patricia from her life-defining memoir Priestdaddy, her devastating yet delirious novels No One Is Talking About This ([Storysmith Book of the Year 2021](https://storysmithbooks.com/list/storysmith-books-of-the-year-2021/)) and Will There Ever Be Another You, her poetry collection Motherland Fatherland Homelandsexuals, or [that video where she slowly extrudes a crystal egg from her mouth](https://x.com/TheBookerPrizes/status/1455100456699670534). We’re very excited.

***Pre-order your copy of Agate Head / Stone Soup** (rrp £18.99) for a special discounted price with your ticket, then collect on the night!*

## About Patricia Lockwood

Patricia Lockwood is the author of six books, including the 2021 novel No One Is Talking About This, an international bestseller which was shortlisted for the Booker Prize and the Women’s Prize for Fiction, and translated into 20 languages. Her 2017 memoir Priestdaddy won the Thurber Prize for American Humor and was named one of the Guardian’s 100 best books of the 21st century. Her other books include the novel Will There Ever Be Another You and two poetry collections, Motherland Fatherland Homelandsexuals (2014) and Balloon Pop Outlaw Black (2012). Lockwood’s work has appeared in the New York Times, the New Yorker, and the London Review of Books, where she is a contributing editor. She lives in Savannah, Georgia.

*Photo credit: Grep Hoax*

## About Agate Head / Stone Soup

Many have called Patricia Lockwood a wordsmith, but in the latest iteration of her life, she has become, quite literally, a metalsmith too. Stones, gems, metals, fossils – she forges them into bodies, faces and, with her typical irreverence, vaginas.

In these poems, a robot dog discovers the Lascaux caves in France. Jane Austen shoots a perfect 147. A rock gets a girlfriend. The Pope blesses McLovin (kind of).

Lockwood’s most successful work of metal- and wordsmithing yet is her blend of the Internet world with the natural one, as she slips meme references and algospeak into evocations of geological time, explorations of organic bodies, and observations of youth. Her most personal collection of poetry yet, you may find you understand yourself – and Patricia – more than you’d like to by the end.

**Join us for an exciting evening to discuss translated literature. Whether you're a fan of literary fiction or just looking to try something new, this book club hopes to achieve just that. **

**In September, we'll be celebrating our book club's two year anniversary! Come along for a mini party and book club discussion that takes a trip down memory lane...**

***Date:***

**THE TWO YEAR BOOK CLUB SPECIAL:**

To celebrate the book club's two year anniversary, we're going to take a trip down memory lane and revisit the books we've explored together in our book club.

The goal is simple: pick your favourite book club title and bring it on the night so we can discuss what we all liked, didn't like, and see what titles we're all fond of.

price.text: £29 includes a copy of the book; £5 admission only

events.raw:
**An Evening with Jonn Elledge** — Thursday 24th September 19:00, Waterstones, Bristol - Galleries.
From electric lighting to pedestrian crossings
events.summary: Jonn Elledge on 31 Inventions that Built Our World — lifts, street lighting, pedestrian crossings — then questions and a signing.
events.description:
For over 10,000 years, we humans have been busy altering our environment and embracing 'progress', evolving seamlessly from hunter gatherers to the modern urban sophisticates we see ourselves as today.

But what are the ideas and inventions that enabled humanity to become, by the early 21st century, a majority urban species for the first time? How did the essential infrastructure of modern life - the innovations that we barely even notice, but without which our world would fall apart - actually come to be?

With his characteristic wit and boundless curiosity, Jonn Elledge invites us to join him on a fascinating and often surprising tour of the ideas and technologies that made modernity possible. From elevators to electric lighting, parks to pedestrian crossings, he guides us through the history of civilisation itself.

Jonn will talk about his new book before an audience Q&A and book signing.

**Jonn Elledge **is the author of the number-one bestseller, *A History of the World in 47 Borders**. *A New Statesman and New World columnist*, *he is a regular on the podcasts *Oh God, What Now? *and the late, lamented *Paper Cuts, *and a frequent contributor to *The i Paper, the Guardian *and assorted other publications. He was previously an assistant editor at the *New Statesman*, where he created and ran its urbanism-focused *City Metric *site, spending six happy years writing about cities, maps and borders and hosting the *Skylines *podcast*. *He has written three books, as well as over 200 editions of the *Newsletter of (Not Quite) Everything*. He lives in London, with the best dog in the world.

**ABOUT THE BOOK**

***BIG LITTLE TRUTHS***

After the lies, come the truths . . .

Ten years ago, at the Pirriwee High School gates, the friendships of Celeste, Jane and Madeline were forged in the fires of young motherhood, the big little lies we all tell to hide our deepest fears and secrets – and the event that changed everything.

Now mothers to hormonal teens, these frazzled friends are starting to worry about the strangers newly occupying their kids’ bedrooms. Or they would, if they weren’t so distracted by their own problems. Because Madeline’s landmark birthday is about to land a bombshell. Jane’s rock-solid marriage is suddenly crumbling. And Celeste’s mother-in-law is asking awkward questions about the past. Not to mention the mystery of who sent the school receptionist a freshly severed finger. So many difficult little truths that each is facing.

Such a pity then that not a one of them can see the biggest ugliest truth hiding in their midst . . .

***Big Little Truths is the sequel to Big Little Lies, the breakout worldwide phenomenon that has sold over 6 million copies and is an Emmy- and Golden Globe-winning HBO sensation, produced by and starring Reese Witherspoon and Nicole Kidman. This novel follows Madeline, Celeste and Jane and their teenage kids years later, and will inspire the upcoming TV series.***

**ABOUT THE AUTHORS**

**Liane Moriarty** is the bestselling author of ten novels, including *Here One Moment*, *Apples Never Fall, The Husband's Secret, Big Little Lies* and *Nine Perfect Strangers*. Her novels have sold more than 25 million copies worldwide and have been translated into over 40 languages. *Big Little Lies* is now an Emmy and Golden Globe-winning HBO series, produced by and starring Nicole Kidman and Reese Witherspoon. *Nine Perfect Strangers* and *Apples Never Fall* have both been adapted for TV. *Here One Moment* is being adapted for TV by Nicole Kidman and Bruna Papandrea. Liane lives in Sydney with her husband, son and daughter.

**Charlotte Philby** is a critically acclaimed author of six novels. As a journalist, she worked for eight years as a newspaper reporter, editor and columnist at the *Independent*, where she was shortlisted for the Cudlipp Prize for investigative reporting. She is a former contributing editor and features writer at *Marie Claire*, and has written for publications including the *Sunday Times, New Statesman* and *Financial Times*. With the support of the BFI, she is currently adapting for film her novel *Edith and Kim*, which reimagines the lives of her grandfather, the double-agent Kim Philby, and Edith Tudor-Hart, who recruited him to the Soviet cause. Charlotte has three children and lives in Bristol.

**Play Fridays** — 25 Sep 2026, 10am - 12pm. Best for ages 0-5.

For families with children under 5, these special sessions once a month are all about
sensory play, having fun and exploratory learning.
events.summary: A monthly morning in the Theatre of Curiosity built for under-fives, each one on a different schema — September's is Rotation, with spinning tops and rolling toys.
events.description:
Relax, play and have fun together in our Play Friday sessions for under 5s and their
grown-ups.

Each month, our Theatre of Curiosity space comes alive with a different mini-adventure
developed specially for our youngest visitors.

Our Play Friday sessions are developed using the theory of schematic play to encourage
open-ended exploration and help children learn about the world through play.

**Upcoming events:** 25 Sept, 6 Nov, 4 Dec.

September's theme is 'On A Roll'. It's time to twist, turn, spin and roll. Experiment with
spinning tops and rolling toys or turn yourself around. This session is based on the Rotation
Schema: where a child is fascinated by objects or their own body spinning, twisting, rolling,
or moving in circles. It helps toddlers and young children develop balance, coordination,
spatial awareness, and an understanding of cause and effect.

**Access considerations** — Play Friday takes place in a large open space in the centre of
the ground floor. On busy days, the space can be noisy. Most activities will be at floor
height and the space can get a bit messy. You can come and go as you please between Play
Friday and the rest of the exhibition.

events.raw:
**Comedy: Stand Up For The Weekend with Mike Gunn & Guests**

26 September · 20:00 – 22:00 · From £12
events.summary: Circuit veteran Mike Gunn headlines, finding dark comedy in family life and middle age.
events.description:
### Stand Up For The Weekend with Mike Gunn Featuring Michelle Shaughnessy plus compere Jeremy Flynn

##### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: MIKE GUNN

Widely regarded as one of the UK’s finest circuit comedians, Mike Gunn blends darkly intelligent observations with a brilliantly understated delivery, finding humour in family life, middle age and the everyday frustrations we can all relate to. A misspent youth and a series of grim jobs cultivated his cynical outlook on life and a perverse desire led him to the world of stand-up. A self-confessed pessimist, he describes himself as “not a natural choice for a career in laughter”. He has a rare ability to walk close to the line of what audiences find acceptable and yet still remain likable and funny. His reputation for being a bit unfriendly, a touch dark and even morose is really not true. In real life he’s loving, warm and philanthropic. Just a bit misunderstood.

#### “*Piercingly funny… fiendishly funny, as dry as a dead man’s bones*.” — The List

#### “*There is plenty of enjoyment to be had in his downbeat meanderings on the futility of life*.” Chortle

#### “*Mike Gunn will make you die laughing*.” — The Guardian

#### Highly Commended Comedy Award — Time Out Dubai

[https://www.mikegunn.co.uk/](https://www.mikegunn.co.uk/)

events.description:
Star of Live At The Apollo, Have I Got News For You, QI, Richard Osman’s House of Games & Comedy Central Live; Ignacio Lopez returns with perhaps his most ambitious and pretentious project yet.

Nada is the captivating comedy experiment which sees Spain’s Best Export create a brand new, completely unique and blisteringly funny stand up show right in front of your eyes, from absolutely nothing!

Mining his hilarious upbringing, growing up in Mallorca and South Wales, as well as suggestions from the crowd, and everything he’s learnt performing comedy since 2010, Ignacio crafts an intricate story of mystery and suspense packed with sarcasm, silliness and huge laughs.

As well as dazzling viewers with his quick-wit and charm on almost every UK TV station, Ignacio’s talents have seen him headlining all the top comedy clubs, cruises, corporate and military shows worldwide and his acclaimed, sold out tour shows all over the UK prove he’s an act not to be missed.

events.title: Mark Thomas: 40 in Stand-Up Years
events.raw:
**Comedy: Mark Thomas – 40 IN STAND-UP YEARS**

30 September · 20:00 – 22:00 · £22
events.summary: Mark Thomas marks four decades at the mic, looking back over a career of comedy and activism.
events.description:
What?! Mark Thomas has been ‘standing up’ for 40 years? Impossible!! But how old does that make you…? Alas it is true; one of our oldest surviving alternative comics celebrates 40 years at the mic.

So, here’s what he has done so far in numbers; performed comedy for 40 years, won 8 awards for performing, 4 for human rights work and 1 he invented for himself, made 6 series of the Mark Thomas Comedy Product (Channel 4), written 6 books and 5 play scripts, made 5 series of the Manifesto for Radio 4, made 3 Dispatches for Channel 4, sued the police (and won) 3 times, curated and authored 2 art exhibitions with artist Tracey Moberly and had 1 Guinness World Record for holding 20 protests in 24 hours.

If that’s not enough, he’s also walked 724km around the length of the Israel Wall in the West Bank, been credited with changing the law on tax avoidance, started a comedy club in Palestine with Dr Sam Beale and campaigned successfully for things like trade union recognition for cinema workers and getting multinationals to change their practices. You’re right, there’s more, but your attention is running out and we’re running out of space. So let’s just say he’s generally mucked about trying to have fun and upset the right people…which he is really, really good at.

So basically expect a taster menu of government and personal mayhem, jokes, rants and a personal state of the nation broadcast as he tries to turn ‘what the f*ck is going on’ into a cogent hour of stand-up.

★★★★★ “*Once again shooting laughter-laden political bullets from the lip*” THE RECS

events.summary: Carey Marx headlines the club night with short, sharp and deliberately uncomfortable gags.
events.description:
## Stand Up For The Weekend with Carey Marx & Guests Featuring Joey Page plus compere Jack Campbell

#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available.

#### Headliner: CAREY MARX

Carey Marx is an unapologetic gagsmith. The jokes are short and sharp, often uncomfortably so, as any morality is sacrificed on the altar of quick laughs. And there’s no better way of guaranteeing a reaction than storming headlong into decidedly dodgy territory.

There’s plenty here for the connoisseur of comedy writing. The lines are efficient, original and potent – and rarely fail to blindside the audience.

And they come at a blistering rate, thanks to a hugely economical delivery. He doesn’t go out of the way to befriend an audience, yet there is a subtle charm and intelligence to him, even when the material is blatantly offensive.

#### “*Hilariously demented*” Edinburgh Evening News

#### “*Anecdotally debauched … But if his lines are frequently sick, they’re elegantly written, too, and there’s a childlike glee to his naughtiness*.” The Herald

https://www.facebook.com/CareyMarxComedy/

# Woodwork for Beginners Level 1 – The Toolbox

This introductory woodworking course teaches students to create a
softwood toolbox with a handle and inset base using traditional hand
tools and corner rebate joints. Upon completion, participants take
home their finished toolbox and gain foundational skills to pursue
home projects or advance to Level 2 classes.

- Sawing straight and square
- Accurately marking out and cutting joints
- Effectively using hand tools including chisels and planes
- Fitting and finishing woodwork projects

events.raw: **Event 06/10: An evening with David McKay, award-winning translator** — From £6.00.
events.summary: What it takes to carry a Dutch novel into English, with David McKay on his translation of Anjet Daanje's The Song of Stork and Dromedary.
events.description:
**We are absolutely delighted to be hosting David McKay, the award-winning translator of Dutch fiction and non-fiction, who will be discussing his latest translation of Anjet Daanje's *The Song of Stork and Dromedary*. This will be a fantastic and riveting evening spent discussing what it takes to bring a Dutch novel into English.**

**Date:**
Tuesday 6th of October

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 19:00. Finish approx 20:00.

**Tickets:**
£6 ticket only
£25 ticket with The Song of Stork and Dromedary (hardback)
£12.99 ticket with The Remembered Soldier (paperback)

You don't need to bring your ticket with you, we will have a list of names on the door. Books will be available to buy on the night.

**ABOUT THE BOOKS**

***The Song of Stork and Dromedary***

**Inspired by the life and work of Emily Brontë, this masterful, multi-award-winning book — acclaimed as the best Dutch novel published this century — pulls readers into a narrative that redefines time itself.**

In the early 1800s, in Yorkshire, Eliza May Drayden and her sisters live far from the public eye, devoted to their shared love of reading and writing books. When, after dozens of rejections, Eliza May’s only novel, *Haeger Mass*, is finally published, it’s labelled as ‘ghastly’ and ‘immoral’. Over time, however, it is embraced by generations of readers as a masterpiece, and tales about its mysterious, reclusive author take on a life of their own.

In eleven extraordinary chapters, the story of Eliza May — both before and after her death — unfolds: through the tales of people who met her; her sister’s letters; her biographers’ words; the pages of a mysterious notebook; and the lives that become intertwined with hers, even centuries later.

In *The Song of Stork and Dromedary*, Anjet Daanje has crafted an absorbing literary mystery and an unforgettable meditation on love, life, loss, and the inexplicable nature of time. As the Brontës themselves did, Daanje shows us that storytelling is our only way to transcend death.

***The Remembered Soldier***

**An extraordinary love story and a captivating novel about the power of memory and imagination.**

Flanders 1922. After serving as a soldier in the Great War, Noon Merckem has lost his memory and lives in a psychiatric asylum. Countless women, responding to a newspaper ad, visit him there in the hope of finding their spouse who vanished in battle. One day a woman, Julienne, appears and recognises Noon as her husband, the photographer Amand Coppens, and takes him home against medical advice. But their miraculous reunion doesn’t turn out the way that Julienne wants her envious friends to believe. Only gradually do the two grow close, and Amand’s biography is pieced together on the basis of Julienne’s stories about him. But how can he be certain that she’s telling the truth?

In *The Remembered Soldier*, Anjet Daanje immerses us in the psyche of a war-traumatised man who has lost his identity. When Amand comes to doubt Julienne’s word, the reader is caught up in a riveting spiral of confusion that only the greatest works of literature can achieve.

*Longlisted for the 2026 International Booker Prize.*

**ABOUT THE TRANSLATOR**

**David McKay** is an award-winning translator of Dutch fiction and nonfiction. Born and educated in the United States, he has lived in and around The Hague since 1997.

events.description:
**Everyone is welcome at our Contemporary Fiction book club, where on the first Wednesday of every month we discuss a recently-published paperback novel. In October, we'll be delving into *Drayton and McKenzie by Alexander Starritt*, a Sunday Times, GQ, and Financial Times 2025 Book of the Year. **

***Date:*
Wednesday 7th of October

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**

Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *Drayton and McKenzie***

**A TIMES/SUNDAY TIMES, GQ, FINANCIAL TIMES AND BLOOMBERG BEST BOOK OF THE YEAR 2025**

*‘A big, bustling novel about love, friendship, money, ambition and the 21st century, packed with humour and intelligent observations … I finished it tear-stained’ Sunday Times*

*‘Will have you hooked … an ode to the enduring power of male friendship’ The Times Best Summer Books*

*‘My book of the summer’ Janice Turner*

*‘Thrilling’ Guardian*

For the first time since university, James and Roland’s paths through life – one drawn in straight lines, the other squiggled and meandering – began to cross…

James Drayton has always found things too easy. By the time he leaves university, he’s still waiting for a challenge worthy of his ambitions. Roland Mackenzie, on the other hand, is an impulsive risk-taker, a charismatic drifter with a knack for derailing his own attempts to get started in life.

When a chance encounter in a pub reunites these old acquaintances, it sets them on an unpredictable course through the upheavals of the twenty-first century, and sparks an unlikely alliance. Sent to Aberdeen during the financial crisis to lay off hundreds of workers, James and Roland begin to wonder: what if they were made for more than this? What if together they could build something grand and lasting – something that might even change the world?

events.raw: **Meg Mason: Sophie, Standing There** — Thursday 8th October 2026, 7pm. £8.00 – £20.00.
events.summary: The author of Sorrow and Bliss on her new novel, with Monica Heisey. Not at the shop — this one is at The Station on Silver Street, and there is a low-income ticket tier.
events.description:
*The Station, Silver Street, Bristol, BS1 2AG ([click here for a map](https://maps.app.goo.gl/3exg7KQv8vD3BaEGA)) For venue access info, [click here](https://www.accessable.co.uk/bristol-city-council/access-guides/the-station).*

We are delighted to welcome the international bestselling author of the seminal novel Sorrow and Bliss, **Meg Mason**, to Bristol this autumn! She’ll be here to discuss her new novel **Sophie, Standing There** with fellow author and chronicler of life’s ineffable difficulties, **Monica Heisey **(author of equally-beloved bestseller [Really Good Actually](https://storysmithbooks.com/product/really-good-actually-2/), writer on Schitt’s Creek).

Sorrow and Bliss won Book of the Year at the British Book Awards, was shortlisted for the Women’s Prize, and has been translated into more than 30 languages. Sophie, Standing There is one of the most anticipated books of the year, and has already won praise from Gillian Anderson and Ann Patchett (no biggie).

**Pre-order your copy of Sophie, Standing There** (rrp £20.00) for a special discounted price with your ticket, then collect on the night!

## About Meg Mason

Meg Mason is the author of You Be Mother and Sorrow and Bliss, which became an international bestseller after it was published in 2021. Winner of the British Book Industry Book of the Year, and shortlisted for the Women’s Prize, it has since been translated into twenty-five languages. Her first career was in journalism, beginning at The Times of London, and later writing for Vogue, Elle, GQ, and humour for the New Yorker’s Daily Shouts. Born in New Zealand, she lives in Sydney with her husband and two daughters.

## About Sophie, Standing There

**From the award-winning, bestselling author of Sorrow and Bliss comes an achingly tender, poignant, funny and bittersweet new novel**

*‘Heartwarming, tender and so funny, Sophie, Standing There is a wonderful, bittersweet story of what it means to be truly, achingly lonely. I loved it’* – Gillian Anderson

*‘So smart, so funny, so moving. I absolutely loved it’* Bonnie Garmus, bestselling author of Lessons in Chemistry

*‘A moving examination of what it means to be alone in the world, and what it means to find connection. It is, by turns, heartbreaking, hilarious, and deeply hopeful. Meg Mason is a dazzling talent’* Ann Patchett, bestselling author of Tom Lake and The Dutch House

Sophie Pattison is a lovely person – warm, kind, relentlessly positive. She’s cherished by her brother Laurie, adored by her best friend Emma and valued by her colleagues. Sometimes, it’s true, one day in her life can feel like the entire month of January. It’s also true she can go an entire day without speaking. But she’s fine really. She spends her time alone reading, finding comfort in the pages of the books she devours.

Until one day she stumbles upon an author she hasn’t read in years. Her books, interviews and podcasts soon become a lifeline; every word is a solace, company she hasn’t felt in so long. It’s almost like love.

A lot like love. And Sophie would love to meet the author, although she never will obviously. In a way, thank goodness, because that would change everything. Sophie’s entire life. Wouldn’t it?

**Hilariously candid and raw, Sophie, Standing There is a bittersweet story of love, loneliness and finding connection in the most unlikely of places.**

*‘Sophie, Standing There unfolds like a strange origami crane in reverse – so achingly tender and so brilliantly subtle that I could never put it down… Dazzling’* Catherine Newman, bestselling author of Wreck and Sandwich

*‘I loved Sophie, and I love Meg Mason’s brain and the strange, wonderful, funny stories she gives us’* Ann Napolitano, bestselling author of Hello, Beautiful and Dear Edward

## About Monica Heisey

Monica Heisey is a writer and comedian from Toronto. She has been published in The New Yorker, The New York Times, Vogue, Elle, The Guardian, Glamour, New York magazine, and VICE, among others. She has written for television shows like Schitt’s Creek, Workin’ Moms, Baroness von Sketch Show, and more. Her debut novel — Really Good, Actually — was published by 4th Estate in 2022 and is a Sunday Times Bestseller. She currently lives in London.

events.raw: **Geology 1979 Reunion** — 9 October 2026, 12.00 PM - 10 October 2026, 5.00 PM. Venue: TBC.
events.summary: Geologists who started in 1979 mark fifty years over two days: Friday lunch, the Geology Department and the Wills Building tower, then on Saturday either the rediscovered caverns under the Clifton Suspension Bridge with a geologist guide, or a walking tour of St Nicholas Market. The venue is still to be confirmed.
events.description:
The Geologists of 1979 are delighted to invite you to a reunion on 9 and 10 October 2026, celebrating 50 years since they started the course.

Their plans include meeting for lunch on the Friday, followed by a visit to the Geology Department and a tour of the Wills Building including a trip up the tower, followed by an evening meal in a restaurant in Bristol.

On Saturday morning there are the possibilities of a trip down to the caverns below the Clifton suspension bridge (only rediscovered about 20 years ago) with a guide who is a geologist or a walking tour of St Nicks market (they will do a poll once they know who is able to come).

Please forward this invitation to any friends who graduated in 1979 that you are still in touch with.

**Contact**

If you are interested in coming, please email the organiser, John Leeson (BSc Geology 1979) at johnleeson@aol.com. Further details will be communicated closer to the time.

This event is organised by alumni volunteers and is independent of the University of Bristol. The University of Bristol does not accept any liability for this event.

"An exciting chance to make some significant records in an extremely

events.summary:
A botany recording meeting in a corner of the city that has almost no records
at all — the target grid square holds a single entry, made by the author of
*The Bristol Flora* in 1898.
events.description:
An exciting chance to make some significant records in an extremely
under-recorded part of town. The monad (1km OS map grid square) that we will
target currently has just a single record to its name in the Botanical Society
of Britain and Ireland's database: Fine-leaved Sandwort _Sabulina tenuifolia_.
And what's more, that record was made in 1898 by none other than the great
J. W. White, author of the seminal The Bristol Flora. Who knows what we might
find?! But two things are for sure:

1) There will be some items of interest

2) Fine-leaved Sandwort is highly unlikely to persist.

2:00pm start. Leader: David Hawkins. Meet at Emerson's Green Common just off
Emerson's Green Lane at ST668768, ///events.ears.brave, postcode BS16 7HB.
Filed by the society under Botany.

What does that first step feel like? How does interacting with someone else make us feel? Why does rolling over feel so good!

Join us as we journey from 0-3 years old, finding our feet, our feelings and our fun. Find a connection whether you have children of your own, or from when you yourself were a child.

Using movement and clowning, *Wonder Baby* invites children and families to explore physical play and experience the joy of creating space to play together.

Grown from the imaginations and experiences of babies, toddlers and their families – *Wonder Baby* was developed in collaboration with families who took part in the early development of the show.

events.summary: Two halves of unscripted comedy in the Chicken Shed: audience-prompted improv games, then a guest two-prov set.
events.description:
Wednesday Night Improv returns to the Hen & Chicken with two halves of unscripted comedy – all made up on the spot, all inspired by your suggestions. Expect quick wit, bold characters, and the kind of laughter that only happens when nobody knows what’s coming next (including the performers).

**## FIRST HALF ##Comedy Games, Improvised Live**

*(Think Whose Line Is It Anyway? meets Game Changer, with a sprinkling of Taskmaster.)*

A fast, funny first half built around short improvised games – the kind where performers get a prompt from the audience and have seconds to turn it into something brilliant. Points will be awarded. Consequences may follow.

With your host, Ste Brown.

**## SECOND HALF ##The BLANK Who BLANKED Me**

Love stories are with us from a very young age, usually stories of love that is pure and sweet and true. *The BLANK who BLANKED me* is not that kind of love story.

This is the kind of love story where passion strikes like a wrecking ball, leaving you dazed, confused, and madly in love with an unaccountable asshole who does admittedly look really good climbing out of a lake in a thin white shirt…

—

Whether you’re a seasoned comedy fan or just curious about what happens when performers make it all up as they go, this is a perfect night to dive into Bristol’s thriving improv scene. Expect laughter, surprises, and something completely different — every single time.

—

*Part of the Wednesday Night Improv series – second Wednesday of every month.* *Details: https://linktr.ee/wednightimprov*

**What to expect**

- Explore virtual tours of homes that have already been retrofitted

Exhibitors and product demonstrations: To be confirmed.

This event is hosted by Retrofit West and funded by the West of
England Mayoral Combined Authority.

Retrofit West supports homeowners across the West of England to
improve the energy efficiency of their homes through high-quality
retrofit. Their mission is to help accelerate the transition to
low-carbon housing, reducing carbon emissions while creating warmer,
healthier homes, lowering energy costs and supporting local jobs and
skills.

events.description:
Calm Sensory Sessions have been designed for anyone who benefits from visiting at a time
when there is a calmer background sensory environment – particularly neurodivergent people
of all ages.

**What will the sessions include?** We understand that the sensory experience at SS Great
Britain can be challenging for some of our visitors. Where possible these calm sensory
sessions will include:

- Audio, visual, and smell effects will be turned off or reduced.
- Lighting levels will be adjusted.
- Capacity will be reduced.
- Dedicated sensory room.

These sessions will vary throughout the year with some happening on weekends and some
during weekdays in school holidays. Some will be mornings and some afternoons.

**Upcoming dates:** Sunday 17th October 10am-5pm. Sunday 31st January 10am-5pm.

Visual and sensory guides are available to download: Visual Story, Visual Timetable,
Sensory Information Guide, Sounds & Smells Guide and Mannequin Map.

events.title: Greipur Hjaltason: The Icebreaker UK Tour
events.raw:
**COMEDY: GREIPUR HJALTASON – THE ICEBREAKER UK TOUR**

20 October · 20:00 – 22:00 · From £30
events.summary: Iceland's Comedian of the Year, with over two million Instagram followers, on his first UK tour.
events.description:
Greipur Hjaltason — Iceland’s Comedian of the Year 2020 (yes, the competition wasn’t exactly fierce up north 😏) — has rapidly become one of the most recognisable voices in European stand-up comedy. Now, for the very first time, he’s taking his unique brand of humour on tour across the UK , ready to meet the people who helped propel him to international fame.

With over 2 million followers on Instagram, more than 800,000 fans on TikTok, and 1+ billion views, Greipur has taken the internet by storm. His rise began with viral videos featuring his razor-sharp wit, perfectly deadpan delivery, and brutally honest observations on parenting, relationships, and life on a tiny island full of volcanoes, glaciers, and questionable weather choices.

Online he’s known simply as @greipjokes — a comic voice that travels far beyond Iceland. His material leaps from everyday quirks to cultural weirdness, with a twist of Icelandic charm. One moment he’s lecturing about elves, the next he’s dismantling Nordic stoicism — and audiences everywhere crack.

Fresh off his digital domination and a guest spot on the award-winning Comedy Roundtable podcast, Greipur now steps off the screen and onto real stages across the UK. Expect sharp storytelling, sneaky sarcasm, and a mischievously charming presence that’s even better in person.

**From volcanoes and glaciers… to audiences across the UK. Greipur Hjaltason — live, unfiltered, and funnier than ever.**

events.raw: **Event 22/10: Phil Melanson introduces Florenzer** — From £6.00.
events.summary: Phil Melanson on his debut Florenzer, a queer historical novel set in fifteenth-century Florence.
events.description:
**Join us for a fantastic evening with Phil Melanson to discuss his brilliant debut, *Florenzer:* a queer, historical novel that paints a richly imagined portrait of a city that paints over its own decay; where an untested artist, not yet marked by greatness, will dare to follow his most unholy desires.**

**Date:**
Thursday 22nd of October

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 19:00. Finish approx 20:00.

**Tickets:**
£6 ticket only
£14.99 ticket with *Florenzer* (paperback)

You don't need to bring your ticket with you, we will have a list of names on the door. Books will be available to buy on the night.

**ABOUT THE BOOK**

***Florenzer***

*THE DAZZLING NEW HISTORICAL FICTION NOVEL FOR FANS OF THE SONG OF ACHILLES AND MARRIAGE PORTRAIT.*

15th-century Florence: where the river runs red with slaughterhouse blood and bronze statues glow in every square. Into its fold comes a young Leonardo da Vinci. Wayward and dreamy, he is different from the other artists' apprentices, drawn to what passes behind veils of steam in the baths and along the moonlit banks of the Arno.

Such habits have long belonged to Florence, but they carry risk in a city where anonymous accusations slipped into letterboxes destroy reputations overnight. Alongside Leonardo, two men pursue their own forms of immortality: Francesco Salviati, a priest willing to endure any degradation in the name of salvation, and Lorenzo de' Medici, heir to a great banking fortune, for whom wealth proves a shifting, uncertain thing.

Weaving together these three lives, *Florenzer* is a sensuous and richly imagined portrait of a city that paints over its own decay; where an untested artist, not yet marked by greatness, will dare to follow his most unholy desires.

*'The rift between Rome and Florence brings Melanson's three characters together in a bloody, vivid climax. All three characters are superbly drawn and Renaissance Florence leaps from the page...A stunning debut.' - The Times*

*'A captivating portrait of an all-too-human genius - subtle, erudite and exquisitely sexy.' - James Cahill, author of The Violet Hour*

*'Florenzer is a heady, intoxicating debut that examines the meaning of art in a time of turmoil. Melanson draws subtle, intimate portraits of his three protagonists, each of them caught between the worldly and the divine. Tortured Leonardo, ambitious Lorenzo and fanatical Salviati: the lives of these men intersect in surprising and sometimes bloody ways in the cutthroat world of Renaissance Italy. Told in rich, vivid prose, passion and desire permeate every page.' - Danielle Giles, author of Mere*

*'Introduces us to a teenage Leonardo still struggling to find himself amid the roiling artistic and political atmosphere of late-15th-century Florence... For a young man sexually attracted to other young men, this can be particularly dangerous...Yet his work may be his salvation.' - New York Times Book Review*

*'Impressively ambitious. . . An enjoyably sticky web of intrigue is spun, with much gossiping, bribing and backstabbing, and much shifting of allegiance between the great centres of power on the peninsula.' - TLS*

***ABOUT THE AUTHOR***

**Phil Melanson** is the author of the queer historical novel *Florenzer*, which was a National Bestseller, long-listed for the Centre for Fiction’s First Novel Prize, and an Allstora “(Very) Gay Book Club” Selection. He is a graduate of NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts and the University of Warwick, and in another life was a digital marketer for Hollywood film studios, working on campaigns for movies such as *Little Women, Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again *and* Once Upon on a Time… in Hollywood*. He teaches with Boston University in London, where he lives with his husband.

events.description:
*Storysmith, 236 North Street, Bristol, BS3 1JD*

Join us in the shop for a very special book signing with the one and only **Oliver Jeffers**!

Oliver will be joining us to celebrate not only the release of his new picture book **A Day Off School** (written by Oliver and illustrated by Kevin Waldron), but also the new paperback edition of his classic **There’s a Ghost in This House**.

**You’ll get a free art print with every purchase of either of those two books**, and we’ll also have an array of Oliver’s incredible backlist on sale too, ready for him to sign just for you.

Here’s the lowdown on how it’ll work on the day:

- *You must purchase a £5 ticket to attend: this can be redeemed against any Oliver Jeffers book on the day (we’ll have a large selection of his books available as well as the new ones!)*

- *One ticket required per group (up to 5 people)*

- *The signing will begin at 3:30pm and tickets are limited to ensure everyone will have time to get their books signed, but please be aware that you will have to queue!*

## About Oliver Jeffers

Oliver Jeffers’ career in children’s books began with his highly acclaimed debut, How to Catch a Star, first published in 2004. Since then, he has become a worldwide phenomenon and a genre-busting creative force in the world of children’s books with book translations in forty-nine languages. Oliver has exhibited in museums and galleries such as the Brooklyn Museum in New York, the National Portrait Gallery in London and the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in Boston. In 2022 Oliver received a Member of the Order of the British Empire Award (MBE) for his Services in Art and in 2026 Oliver joined Smartphone Free Childhood as their ambassador.

*Photo credit: Caroline Tompkins*

## About A Day Off School

A hilarious story full of action and adventure from two highly regarded, award-winning picture book creators.

When Herbie has the sniffles, he stays home from school. It’s exciting to have time to play Space Blasters and watch cartoons.

But, by lunchtime, he starts to wonder what he might be missing at school. What if there’s an extra playtime, a dog on the loose… or even A PIRATE INVASION?

Is Herbie missing out on all the action? A hilarious, action-packed story from the globally bestselling creator of Lost and Found and Here We Are, Oliver Jeffers, and the award-winning illustrator of Chocolate Cake, Kevin Waldron.

## About There’s a Ghost in This House

*“Hello, come in. Maybe you can help me?”*

A young girl lives in a haunted house, but has never seen a ghost. Are they white with holes for eyes? Are they hard to see? She’d love to know!

Step inside and join in an entertaining ghost hunt, from behind the sofa, right up to the attic. With lots of friendly ghost surprises and incredible mixed media illustrations, this unique and funny book will entertain young readers over and over again!

A perfect Halloween picture book from the New York Times bestselling creator of Here We Are. Oliver Jeffers has sold more than 18 million books worldwide, in 49 languages!

*‘Hauntingly adorable’* Guardian

*‘Another absolute winner from this inventive author’* Daily Mail

*‘Absolutely brilliant’* BookTrust

*‘Thrilling’* Big Issue

[Accessibility information can be found here.](https://storysmithbooks.com/access/)

events.description:
Yoga Foundations Workshop — Breath, Meditation, Posture & Balance

This Yoga Foundations workshop offers time and space to explore yoga
from the ground up.

We'll work with the four core parts of yoga — Breath, Meditation,
Asana (postures) and basic Philosophy — with a particular focus on
standing postures and balance, including Warrior I, II, III & IV, and
a small number of balance poses.

We'll take our time and work carefully, starting with the basics:

- where to place your feet
- how to breathe within the postures
- how the body organises itself to stand and balance

Alongside the physical learning, we'll explore the essence of these
postures — "what do you stand up for?" "What do you show up for?"

With 2.5 hours together (10:00–12:30), there is space to explore,
explain, rest & repeat – so learning has time to settle and
integrate.

The workshop finishes with Chinese tea for contemplation and light
snacks, offering a gentle close to the morning.

**Make a day of it?** Stay on site for brunch at the excellent
Cibomatto Italian Canteen, book in advance for the sauna and cold
plunge, or head out for a walk in the beautiful Nightingale Valley or
along the river towards Crews Hole.

**Why St Anne's House?**

- Free on-site parking (including accessible spaces)
- Accessible ground-floor Mill Room with step-free access
- Bristol Community Sauna & Cold Plunge on site for post-class
  relaxation
- A vibrant community hub with creative studios, café, and local
  projects

**What to Bring** — Wear comfortable clothes you can move in. Bring
your own yoga mat and props if you have them, plus a blanket and
pillow for relaxation. Mats are available to borrow if needed.

**ABOUT *Dream Count***

**THE INSTANT SUNDAY TIMES NO.1 BESTSELLER; LONGLISTED FOR THE WOMEN'S PRIZE FOR FICTION**

*'Magnificent' SUNDAY TIMES*

*‘Extraordinary’ NEW STATESMAN*

*'The return of a literary titan' TELEGRAPH*

A searing, exquisite novel by the bestselling and award-winning author of Americanah and We Should All Be Feminists – the story of four women and their loves, longings and desires.

Chiamaka is a Nigerian travel writer living in America. Alone in the midst of the pandemic, she recalls her past lovers and grapples with her choices and regrets. Zikora, her best friend, has been successful at everything until – betrayed and brokenhearted – she must turn to the person she thought she needed least. Chiamaka’s bold, outspoken cousin Omelogor is a financial powerhouse in Nigeria who begins to question how well she knows herself. And Kadiatou, Chiamaka’s housekeeper, is proudly raising her daughter in America – but faces an unthinkable hardship that threatens all she has worked to achieve.

Dream Count is Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie’s searing, unforgettable story of these four women – a sparkling, transcendent novel that takes up the very nature of love itself.

events.description:
#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: GARRETT MILLERICK

Garrett Millerick is an acclaimed stand up comedian, writer and director. His unique and versatile style has led to him being in great demand on the alternative and club circuits both in the UK and internationally.

Garrett is known for his grumpy, grouchy persona who is fed up with the pretenses of the modern world, aiming his criticism at everything from the fraudulent activity of the recycling industry to growing depression inflicted by miserablist, oversharing celebrities. His shouty, ironic delivery keeps you on the edge of your seat and the crushing punchlines can leave you exhilarated as he rages against yet more societal hypocrisies.

#### “*Stand up with an insolent twist*” The Sunday Times

events.description:
#### Stand Up For The Weekend with Ali Woods & Guests Featuring Harriet Dyer plus compere Adam Beardsmore

##### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: ALI WOODS

Ali Woods is a half-English, half-Scottish comedian, podcaster and content creator. Ali is a refreshing mix of the ‘every man’ and the ‘modern man’, whose sensitivity and genuine interest in men’s mental health gives him a great perspective on the modern ‘lad’ culture which often features in his comedy. Ali is that wonderful blend of comedy with a heart, speaking on topics such as football, the environment, and many social causes close to his heart.

His online comedy sketches under the tag @aliwoodsgigs have gained millions of views and likes, and featured on LadBible and Buzzfeed UK. In 2022, he supported Russell Kane and Axel Blake on tour and in 2024 supported Adam Kay.

In 2024, Ali starred on Comedy Central Live and Stand Up Sketch Show. He also had a third sold out Edinburgh run with his show ‘At the Moment’ he then embarked on his first ever solo tour across the UK and Ireland to sold-out audiences, including a date at Bristol’s Hen & Chicken.

#### “*Ali Woods is a simply brilliant storyteller*” Everything Theatre

#### “*In a world of wannabes, Woods is the real deal.*” London Evening Standard

**Comedy: The Dark Room with John Robertson**

15 November · 20:00 – 22:00 · £17.50
events.summary: A live-action video game in its thirteenth year: John Robertson traps the audience in a dungeon, and they shout their way out. Sold out.
events.description:
Welcome to **THE DARK ROOM** – the legendary interactive comedy show that fuses improv, crowdwork and gaming to create an insane live-action videogame!

#### “*A Rocky Horror for nerds… reader, I howled*” Daily Telegraph

Now its 13th year, this high-octane interactive show is the brainchild of comedian & cult leader **John Robertson**. Filled with stand-up, appalling prizes and more audience chanting than you’d get at a protest – The Dark Room is a gut-busting rock n’ roll comedy experience for everyone who buys a ticket.

#### “*Will have you crying with laughter*”★★★★★ Broadway Baby

Permanently on tour The Dark Room has headlined stages at Glastonbury, PAX, Download Festival, MCM Comic Con, Utrecht International Comedy Festival 2000 Trees, UK Games Expo and Bluedot Festival, and sold out at Edinburgh Fringe, Soho Theatre and hundreds of theatres around the world.

Oh, and videos of The Dark Room roasting videogames and swearing at children keep popping up on people’s social media, which is nice.

Come watch, and if you want – play – the choose-your-own-adventure madness!

The crowd is trapped inside an inescapable dungeon with a sadistic videogame boss!

Pick increasingly surreal options off the screen and try to escape!

If you win – you get money!

If you fail – YA DIE! YA DIE! YA DIE!

Now, will you:

Find the Light Switch

Go North?

Abandon Hope?

Be sworn at by a man wearing spiked armour and a lot of leather?

(This option is permanently set to “On”)

**WINNER Chortle AwardRUNNER- UP NextUp Biggest Award in ComedyVIRAL AS HELL TikTok, Instagram SOLD OUT – Edinburgh Fringe 2019, 2022, 2023 & 2024**

#### “*NOT TO BE MISSED*” The Guardian

events.raw: **Romance Book Club 30/11: The Love Hypothesis by Ali Hazelwood** — From £0.00.
events.summary: November's romance club leaves Prythian for Ali Hazelwood's The Love Hypothesis.
events.description:
**Whether you’re a fan of the series or looking to delve into romance fiction, our Romance book club offers a joyful escape. We're building a community to gush over swoon-worthy characters and a safe space to discuss themes like relationships. **

**In November, we will be looking at *The Love Hypothesis *by Ali Hazelwood. Let’s share the love!**

**Date:**
Monday 30th of November

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**
Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *THE BOOK***

***The Love Hypothesis***

**When a fake relationship between scientists meets the irresistible force of attraction, it throws one woman’s carefully calculated theories on love into chaos.**

As a third-year Ph. D. candidate, Olive Smith doesn’t believe in lasting romantic relationships but her best friend does, and that’s what got her into this situation. Convincing Anh that Olive is on her way to a happily ever after was always going to be tough, scientists require proof. So, like any self-respecting woman, Olive panics and kisses the first man she sees.

That man is none other than Adam Carlsen, a young hotshot professor and well-known ass. Which is why Olive is positively floored when he agrees to keep her charade a secret and be her fake boyfriend. But when a big science conference goes haywire and Adam surprises her again with his unyielding support (and his unyielding abs), their little experiment feels dangerously close to combustion.

Olive soon discovers that the only thing more complicated than a hypothesis on love is putting her own heart under the microscope.

**ABOUT THE AUTHOR**

**Ali Hazelwood** is an Italian romance novelist and neuroscience professor based in the United States. Many of her works center on women in STEM fields and academia. Her debut novel, The Love Hypothesis, was a New York Times best seller and is currently being developed into a feature film.

events.summary: An extra show added for Ian Stone, whom The Times called a masterful exponent of self-mocking Jewish humour.
events.description:
#### EXTRA SHOW DUE TO POPULAR DEMAND

***“Life can’t just be the humdrum, the mundane and the routine before the inevitable slide to disease, decay and death. Why can’t we sneak in a bit of awesome, a tad of amazing and maybe a smidge of wonderful? A forest canopy opening onto a huge vista would be enchanting for some but my ancestors wandered in the desert for forty years, I think we’ve been outdoors enough. Others get their fix from the spiritual but I’ve been harbouring a grudge against God since my mother stopped me going to Arsenal after my Barmitzvah. Forty nine years ago. ’God will be watching’ she said. Well, at least he got to see the game. The point is, life could be so much better so I’m on the lookout. Come and join me on the hunt.”***

Ian Stone is a hugely experienced broadcaster, podcaster and writer and a brilliantly funny comedian. He performs at major comedy festivals and venues globally. His popular posts and reels on social media have quickly earned him a following of over 60k across BlueSky, Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook, amassing millions of views.

In the last three years, Ian has performed his one-man shows at the Edinburgh Festival to packed rooms and great reviews. In 2023, he won the prestigious Spirit of the Fringe Award. He took his last show on tour across the UK, finishing with a sold-out performance at London’s Comedy Store. Ian recently returned from making his debut at the Melbourne Comedy Festival. He will be returning to Edinburgh with Looking for the Wow before kicking off his UK tour.

Aside from stand-up comedy, Ian co-hosted the award-winning Rock ‘N’ Roll Football show on Absolute Radio for five years with Ian Wright. He currently presents a very popular (50k downloads per episode), twice-weekly Arsenal podcast, Handbrake Off, for The Athletic. A live version of the podcast recently sold out Leicester Square Theatre in London. Ian is also a regular contributor on Times Radio. His book To Be Someone was published in 2020 and has received nearly 500 four- and five-star reviews on Amazon.

Matt Stellingwerf’s comedy blends sharp intellect with warm, conversational storytelling, drawing on his background in criminology, anthropology and life as a New Zealander navigating Britain. He tackles subjects from politics and psychology to relationships and human behaviour with self-deprecating wit and effortless charm.

Highly regarded by his peers, Matt Stellingwerf has won four NZ Comedy Guild Awards, including Best Newcomer. He is now UK based and respected nationwide by promoters and comedy venues.

A renowned MC and compere, Matt is a 3-time nominee for Best MC in New Zealand. Matt was a 2015 and 2016 nominee for the prestigious Billy T Award.

#### Headliner: DAN TIERNAN

Dan Tiernan’s comedy is a thrilling collision of anarchic physicality, razor-sharp writing and disarming vulnerability. He storms the stage with explosive, unpredictable energy, turning stories about addiction, neurodiversity, identity and working-class life into relentless laugh generators. His style veers from absurd one-liners to confessional storytelling, always delivered with a mischievous grin that makes chaos feel joyfully controlled. Critics have praised his ***“dynamic force”* (The Skinny)**, ***“unique ferocity… in utter command”* (Chortle)**, and ***“crude comedy with a big payoff” *(The Guardian)**. The result is exhilarating stand-up that feels dangerous, heartfelt and utterly original, leaving audiences laughing, wincing and wanting more.

Dan made a big impact on the UK comedy circuit back in 2022 after winning both the **BBC New Comedy Award **and the **British Comedian Of The Year**, and if this wasn’t enough he was winner of the **Best Newcomer at the ISH Comedy Awards** in 2023 and nominated for **Best Newcomer at the Edinburgh Festival** the same year. Since then, Dan has also been nominated for the **Next Big Thing** by the British Comedy Guide in 2025. With all of these accolades it does make you wonder where Dan can go from here.

Dan is hugely in demand and has performed at the **Melbourne Comedy Festival**, the **Cat Laughs Comedy Festival** in Ireland, and the **BBC Comedy Festival**, and has appeared on various radio and TV shows including **The Last Leg**, **Live At The Apollo**, **8 Out Of 10 Cats does Countdown**, and **The Stand Up Sketch Show**.

events.title: Christmas Murder Mystery Evening

address.street: Great Western Dockyard, Gas Ferry Road

events.raw:
19 December 2026

**Christmas Murder Mystery Evening** — Take part in an exhilarating evening of
entertainment on board the captivating SS Great Britain.
events.summary: A three-course festive dinner on board that turns into a whodunnit — the strange case of Santa's 'Claws', set at a snowbound school board meeting in Christmas 1937.
events.description:
Take part in an exhilarating evening of entertainment on board the captivating SS Great
Britain. During your dinner, keep your eyes open for clues as you become the detective and
help solve the mysterious crime. We offer guests the ultimate, memorable evening.

**The plot** — Introducing the strange case of Santa's 'Claws'…

Christmas 1937. Mr Uffton Harlecombe had just left the December meeting of the Board of
Governors at St David's School. However, there was very little 'Christmas cheer' at the
meeting this evening. In fact, as he pulled his thick coat tightly around him to shield him
from the silently falling snow, he smiled to himself. He had left no one at that meeting in
any doubt that crossing him was not a smart career move.

Still laughing to himself, he crossed the road and walked along the snow-covered side
street back to his Bentley Sports motor car. Everywhere was silent; a chill wind suddenly
picked up, making him huddle in a doorway to light his cigar. Perhaps he may have seen the
white-bearded face and the crimson costume for a fleeting second. Maybe he even saw the
weapon—a wicked steel claw!

Uffton Harlecombe had misjudged tonight's meeting. The information he had spilt to the
assembled people had been taken far more to heart than he could ever have imagined. One
person would make this a Christmas everyone wants to forget. The spirit of Christmas may
never die, but there are people here tonight who are going to do just that!!

**Key info** — Price: £99pp. Time: 6.30pm-12am. Includes: arrival drink, 3 course festive
menu & murder mystery experience. Group bookings: for tables of 8, contact
events@bristoldockyards.org.

events.summary:
Charlie Harpur, head gardener at the Knepp Estate, on rewilding Knepp's walled
garden and building its market garden — the January instalment of the Friends'
Winter Lectures, in the city centre rather than at the garden.
events.description:
Friends' Winter Lectures will take place on the third Thursday of the month at
the Frank Theatre, Wills Physics Laboratory, Tyndall Avenue, Bristol BS8 1TL
at 7:30pm. Lectures are free to Friends on production of their membership card,
and free to students on production of their student card. Guests who are not
members or students will be asked for a donation (suggested £5).

Speaker: Charlie Harpur, Head Gardener, Knepp Estate.

Charlie joined the Knepp team as Head Gardener in early 2022 to oversee the
rewilding of Knepp's Walled Garden, as well as the development of the Market
Garden and the landscape at the Wilding Kitchen. Having trained as an
architect, he worked for landscape architect Tom Stuart-Smith for several
years, then gained practical experience in horticulture and ecology at Chelsea
Physic Garden and Kew, where he completed the Kew Diploma in Horticulture.

events.description:
Travelling Light in partnership with Alibi present *The Forest Door*.

We are currently making plans and fundraising to tour the show to primary schools in Bristol, Bath and surrounding areas, plus Exeter and the South West in autumn 2027.

**About the show**

What happens when you go through a mysterious portal into another world? On the other side you find yourself in a magical forest, alive with wonder and excitement. Here, you'll meet other enchanting creatures preparing for a big festival… but there is a problem.

Join us on this brand-new adventure, as we explore traditions, memories and solve problems; resulting in one unforgettable celebration.

*The Forest Door* is a new theatre offer for primary aged children, incorporating performance, interactive in-classroom activities, and support and resources for teachers and families.

Grown from the imaginations of young people – The Forest Door is based on ideas from local children who took part in the development in Bristol and Exeter.

**Booking The Forest Door**

To place a booking request for autumn 2027, please complete our School Booking Request Form. Suitable for all primary aged children and their families aged 4-11 (targeted at Reception - Year 4). Performance: 50 mins. Full experience: 2 hours.

**At A Glance:** 27 September - 10 December 2027. Primary schools and community spaces across the South West. No public tickets currently available.

Bedminster Winter Lantern Parade is the biggest creative community event in
South Bristol bringing thousands of local residents together to celebrate
BS3's creativity.

Each Autumn, we hold lantern-making workshops for schools, community groups

bringing thousands of spectators to Bedminster.

The event is organised by a small volunteer Steering Group who work
tirelessly each year to secure the funding and plan the Parade, supported by
200 wonderful volunteers who provide logistical support on the day.

Subject to funding, the parade will go ahead on a Saturday in January 2027.

Looking to sponsor the Bedminster Winter Lantern Parade? Email us at
hellobemmylanterns@gmail.com for more info.

If you'd like to join the organising team and have events, health and
safety, or community outreach experience, we'd love to hear from you.

And we'd also love to hear from community and street groups in BS3 who want
to take part in the next Lantern Parade.

events.description:
Each winter, we offer 1-day workshops teaching traditional hedgelaying: a craft
that preserves the past and protects the future. Courses are taught by
professional hedgelayers and accommodate all skill levels, from beginners to
experienced enthusiasts.

Hedgelaying involves partially severing the stem of the trees in the hedgerow,
allowing them to be laid at an angle of around 45 degrees. This fills gaps in
the hedge while encouraging new vertical shoot growth for denser coverage. The
laid hedge is secured with stakes and binding, varying by regional style.
Previously taught styles include North Somerset and Midland approaches, and
examples of the various techniques can be seen around the Grow Wilder site.

**Winter 2026/27 Dates To Be Announced.** "Future hedgelaying course dates will
be displayed in this section, once confirmed."

Grow Wilder, 181 Frenchay Park Road, Bristol, BS16 1EL. Toilets, picnic area,
accessible toilet and baby changing available; assistance dogs only.
