events.summary: A volunteer-run weekly craft and art meet-up, free and drop-in, with a theme each week but room to bring your own project — set up for people who wanted somewhere creative to go during school hours.
events.description:
Join our weekly creative meet-up group set up by a local volunteer
Elisha.

This is a space to explore art, crafts, and get creative. Everyone is
welcome—whether you're looking to try something new, have a project
in mind, want to meet new people in your local area, or just need
some 'you' time. No artistic experience is needed, but if you have
skills to share, that's great too. As a new group, we'll decide what
we want to explore. Welcoming all ideas and creating projects we can
learn together!

Every Tuesday, 9.30am–11am.

"I've set this up because I love being creative, whether that's
getting my paints out, crafting things with my kids, crocheting or
making presents. After speaking to other parents, I realised that my
desire to have a creative meeting space, open during school hours,
was something others would also enjoy. Knowing this, it inspired me
to create one. So the plan is to create a relaxed space for anyone
who wants to join…Parent or not." – Elisha

We will set up a theme for each session, where I can give inspiration
and projects everyone can get involved in. There will be a WhatsApp
group set up to share ideas and inspiration. The aim is to provide a
creative space where we can all explore in a safe, relaxed & friendly
way. But please also feel free to bring any projects you're working
on, your work may inspire us.

Sessions are free and open to those aged 18 and over, no booking
necessary.

If you have a small child, you're welcome to bring them along, as
long as you're still able to participate fully in the session. The
focus is on taking time for yourself, so we ask that you judge
whether you can take part with your child alongside.

We know it can be hard to anticipate, so you are welcome to come
along and test it out!

events.description:
# Woodwork for Beginners Level 2 – The Lidded Box

Build on your Level 1 skills and apply them to more challenging
joinery. This course teaches you to make a lidded box using black
cherry hardwood and a wide variety of hand joinery techniques.

Upon completion, you will take home a versatile hardwood box with
hinged lid and possess the hand joinery skills to either start making
more advanced projects at home or join level 3 project classes to make
furniture to your own design.

**LEARN HOW TO:**

- Tune and use hand tools effectively
- Accurately mark out, cut & fit a wide variety of hand joinery
  including rebate, through housing, through dovetail, mitre, and
  stopped haunched mortice and tenon
- Fit hinges
- Assemble, glue, cramp and finish your project

Extensions for faster paced woodworkers include half lap mitre and
stopped housing.

**Skill level:** "2 - Suitable for those who have completed our
Woodwork for Beginners Level 1 course."

**Course options:**

- Thursday or Friday daytime classes 10.30am - 3.40pm
- Wednesday or Thursday evening classes 6.20 - 8.45pm
- Weekend daytime classes 10.30am - 4.40pm

events.summary: The longer of the two Level 2 courses: three modules building a softwood cabinet with a fitted drawer and a shaker door, covering housing, dovetail and mortice-and-tenon joints.
events.description:
# Woodwork for Beginners Level 2 – The Cabinet

Make a softwood cabinet with a drawer and shaker style door using
rebate, housing, dovetail and mortice & tenon joints. At the end of
the 3 modules, you will take home your finished cabinet and the skills
& confidence to start designing & making your own woodwork projects.

**LEARN HOW TO:**

- Select, tune and use hand tools effectively
- Accurately mark out, cut & fit a range of traditional joints
- Assemble, glue & cramp projects

**Course structure** — split into three modules:

- **Module 2A - The Case** — joints: through housing, through wedged
  mortice & tenon.
- **Module 2B - The Drawer** — joints: dovetail, corner rebate and
  ploughed groove.
- **Module 2C - The Door** — joints: haunched stopped mortice & tenon
  and ploughed groove.

This course is the lengthier of the level 2 courses. There are more
opportunities for practice and you learn to fit a drawer and a door.
If you would prefer a shorter course, the alternative "Woodwork for
Beginners Level 2 - The Box" course covers broadly the same joinery
techniques.

**Skill level:** Suitable for those who have completed the Woodwork
for Beginners Level 1 course.

**Course options:**

- Thursday or Friday daytime classes 10.30am - 3.40pm
- Wednesday or Thursday evening classes 6.20 - 8.45pm

events.description:
# Woodwork Level 3 – Furniture Projects

Woodwork Level 3 – Furniture Projects is a course focused on planning
and creating furniture or other woodwork projects under tutor
guidance. Participants select their own project, and instructors guide
them through the complete process: planning joinery, making drawings,
sourcing timber, and constructing the project in the workshop.

The course emphasizes hand tools and traditional joinery techniques.
While The Makershed owns hobby-sized power tools, Level 3 woodworkers
may use these only when hand tools would be impractical. See the Power
Tools Policy for details.

**What you'll learn:**

- Plan your own project
- Choose appropriate timber and joinery methods
- Add new joints to your skillset

**Course duration** — Furniture projects vary significantly in
completion time. Since students have completed Levels 1 and 2, they
understand that hand-made furniture requires time and patience. The
number of classes needed depends on your specific project and working
speed.

**Skill level** — Level 3 is suitable for those who have completed
Woodwork for Beginners Level 1 and one Woodwork for Beginners Level 2
course.

**Course options:**

- Thursday or Friday daytime classes 10.30am - 3.40pm
- Wednesday or Thursday evening classes 6.20 - 8.45pm

events.description:
## Discover Bristol's Vibrant Finzels Reach Market

Step into a world of incredible street food at Finzels Reach Market.

Open every Wednesday and Friday lunchtime, discover street food from around
the world.

## Our traders

Where would we be without our wonderful traders? Whilst some loyal traders
have been with us since the start; we're committed to keeping things exciting
by rotating traders each week and inviting guest traders to join us to bring
variety.

We rigorously vet our traders to not only ensure they're turning out the
tastiest street food but to check they are minimalizing food waste and using
eco-friendly packaging.

Want to know who's trading each week? Sign up to our weekly newsletter and
get details of who's trading each week into your in-box every Monday.

## History of Finzels Reach Market

Founded 9 years ago by Sophie Bowden and David Pyne, Finzels Reach Market
opened whilst Finzels Reach was still in development and has become part of
the make-up of this exciting and vibrant quarter. Located on a site which was
once the home to Courage Brewery and previously George's Brewery; the market
has gone through quite the journey. Having launched whilst the area was still
a building site; the market reopened during lockdown covid secure and has
since grown from a weekly market to a successful twice weekly market
showcasing over 40 different traders every month.

The market is carefully curated meaning traders change twice weekly resulting
in an ever-changing selection of street food on offer. Look out for guest
traders, seasonal food and themed markets.

## Visit us

A short walk from the city centre, Finzels Reach Market is located opposite
Castle Park surrounded by independent restaurants, cafes and bars and even
its own brewpub. Find the market located in Old Temple Street just off
Counterslip.

There are 3 routes into the market on foot, via Bath Street, Hawkins Lane
(over Castle Bridge) and Counterslip. Parking is available nearby at The
Galleries and Gardiner Haskins. There is free bike parking in and around
Finzels Reach, with major bike lanes along Counterslip. Many bus services
pass near the market, including the MetroBus. The market is only a 10 minute
walk from Bristol Temple Meads Station. Bristol Ferry runs a waterbus service
which stops at Castle Park jetty, just a minute's walk to the market.

## Frequently asked questions

**What sort of food can you expect at the market?** "With plently of options
for vegan, veggie and meat eaters; the market line-up changes twice weekly to
provide an ever-changing selection" — sushi, fried chicken wings, Thai curry,
Filipino spring rolls, Greek gyros. "For those with a sweet tooth, we always
have a cake stall!"

**How sustainable is the market?** "All of our traders use biodegradable
packaging and we don't allow any single use plastic." Customers are welcome to
bring their own containers.

**When is the market open?** "The market is open all year round on Wednesday
and Friday from 11am - 2pm." It closes at Christmas, New Year and Good Friday.

**Are there toilet facilities?** "As an outdoor pop-up market, unfortunately
we're unable to provide toilets." Public toilets are available at the nearby
Galleries Shopping Centre.

**Do you cater for customers with food allergies?** "All traders have an
ingredient and allergen list available on their stall."

**Is the market family friendly?** "We welcome all customers to the market
whether you bring the kids or a furry friend."

Bristol.

**The only way is up** — Each session lasts roughly 30 minutes and is limited to two
climbers at a time. You'll be guided through every step by trained instructors from Young
Bristol's Outdoor Employment Programme. We're proud to support the youth-driven charity in
its mission to help young locals develop leadership skills and gain nationally recognised
qualifications. They'll make sure you're safe at all times, in an experience we promise is
as authentic as the mid-19th century.

**Key info** — Time: 10.15am–4.15pm. Price: add Go Aloft when booking your General
Admission ticket; £35.00 for the Go Aloft bundle (day pass + Go Aloft), or from £24 per
participant for annual ticket holders. Suitable for families, 10 and over.

Booking in advance is required; there may be walk-up slots on the day for admission ticket
holders but this is not guaranteed, and a waiver form must be completed. Sensible clothing
and closed-toe shoes are required, long hair tied back, jewellery and scarves removed, and
loose items including mobile phones are not permitted on the climb. The full experience
typically lasts 20–30 minutes including the fitting of safety equipment. Climbs take place
in all conditions unless the weather poses a health and safety risk — generally winds
consistently above 20mph, gusts above 30mph, or lightning. Once booked, tickets are
non-transferable and cannot be rescheduled, refunded or cancelled.

events.summary: The city's best-known parkrun: a free timed 5k every Saturday morning on the Ashton Court Estate, ten minutes from the centre across the Avon. Walk it, run it or volunteer; register once online and bring a barcode. Coffee afterwards at the Coach House Café.
events.description:
### What is Ashton Court parkrun?

A free, fun, and friendly weekly 5k community event. Walk, jog, run, volunteer or
spectate – it's up to you!

### When is it?

Every Saturday at 9:00am.

### Where is it?

The event takes place at the Ashton Court Estate, just across the River Avon from Bristol
city centre.

### What does it cost to join in?

Nothing - it's free! but please register before you first come along. Only ever register
with parkrun once and don't forget to bring a scannable copy of your barcode. If you forget
it, you won't get a time.

### How fast do I have to be?

We all take part for our own enjoyment. Please come along and join in whatever your pace!

### We're friendly!

Please join us for a post run coffee at the Coach House Café in the courtyard of Ashton
Court mansion.
